Takachiho Temple monument = The monument built as the place where the metropolitan once stood. == 4.Rituals == The annual festivals held at Kagoshima Shrine are as follows Nanakusamatsuri (January 7) A Shinto ritual to offer rice gruel with seven herbs on the seventh day of the New Year to the gods to bring in the New Year. [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/初午祭_(鹿児島神宮) Hatsuumasai] (nearest Sunday to January 18 of the old calendar) The origin of the Hatsuuma sai is said to have been inspired by a dream that Shimazu Takahisa, then lord of Kagoshima in the Muromachi period (1336-1573), had while overseeing renovation work on the Kagoshima Shrine, while sleeping in the palace. Fujimatsuri (March 10 of the Old calendar) It's a festival of flowers Otauematsuri (May 5 of the Old calendar) The Otaue matsuri is an event held at temples, shrines, and imperial rice paddies. Reisai (August 15 of the Old calendar) Rei sai is the most important of the annual rituals held at shrines. Tanabata (July 7) It celebrates the meeting of the deities Orihime and Hikoboshi. Ohamaori sai ((Third Sunday in October)) The parade of about 350 people, including portable shrines, warriors, gunmen, priestesses, and children, is led by a masked Sarutahiko mikoshi (portable shrine) amidst the sounds of traditional Japanese music. == 5.Cutural treasures == Important cultural property (Registered by government) ・Kagoshima jingu 3bildings   - main shine and worship hall   - imperial messenger's palace   - four auxiliary shines Konito odoshi yoroi (yoroi=armer) including helme and Osode (Registered in 1953 March 31) - Dedication from Kabayama Yoshihisa who was chief retainer of Shimazu cran.    (registered in 1953 March 31) ・Iroiro odoshi doumaru including helmet and Osode (Artifact)   -  Dedication from Shimazu Takahisa in 1558.     (loged in [[Reimeikan, Kagoshima Prefectural Center for Historical Material|Reimeikan]])     (registered in 1953 March 31) ・Iroiro odoshi doumaru (=armer) including helmet and Osode (Artifact)   - Dedication from Shimazu Takahisa in 1558.    (lodged in Tokyo National Museum)    (registered in 1953 March 31) ・Japanese sword:No title wrought by Norishige    -  Although it had been lost since it was requisitioned by the occupation force in post-war,       the sword which the feature matched with this one was found in Australia in 2022.    (registered in 1918,April 8) Japanese sword:Mei toku san wrought by Sousyuzyu Akihiro  -  It was wrought in 1392. Dedication from Shimazu Nariakira who was the twenty seventh       head boss of Shimazu cran.  -  Although it had lost since it was requisitioned by the occupation force in post-war, it was       found in an auction and then Kagoshima jin-gu repurchased it in 2003.     (logged in Reimeikan)     (registered in 1927 April 25) ○Historic site ・Osumi syou hatimangu site and the former site of Syake    (in 2013 October 17) Cultural property designated by Kagoshima prefecture ・Tangible cultural property 　↳・Stone garden lantern which was symbol of reconstruction of Syougu  (Construction)        (registered in 2014 April 22) 　↳・Ceramics owned by Kagoshima-jingu(Aartifact) 　　- it was designated  as tangible cultural property designated by         Kirishima city.(in 2008 March 25)       - it was designated  as tangible cultural property designated by         Kagoshima prefecture.(in 2010 April 23) Document of Kagoshima-jingu (Ancient writing document)       - The letter of appointment for Syou hachimangu shinkan myubu syoku, edict from a         senior official of syou hatimangu syuin, The letter of appointment to Sakai         Tameharu for syo hatimangu miya syurizyo syoku         (registered in 1987 March 16) ・Tengible folk cultural property 　↳ ・Miyauti no ta no kami         (registered in 1968 March 29) Cultural property designated by Kirishima city ・Tangible cultural property 　↳・Tsuji no tuno no hosyoku shurine(building)       - it was formerly Benzaitendo surrounded by Shirasagi lake beside Mirokuin temple. It         was moved to the present site because of the abolition of Buddhism in　 　     Meiji(1868~1912).        (designated in 2005 July 6) 　↳・Statue of the Kagoshima-jingu four devas (historical referense) 　　- It was found in the site of the present Hayato historical folk museum.                 (lodged there) 　　  (designated in 1994 June 7) 　↳・Jingu old stamp(histric referense) 　　 (designated in 1995 July 3) ・Historic site ↳・Miyasaka shell mound   - it was found in Ura sando.     (designated in 1995 December 8) ・Intangible folk cultural property ↳・Horse of 18th day     (designated in 1987 March 31) == 6. [[Kagoshima Prefecture|Kagoshima]] 899-5116 | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Kagoshima Shrine'''|鹿児島神宮|''Kagoshima-jingū''}} is a Shinto shrine located in [[Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]], [[Kagoshima prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is dedicated to [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Emperor Chūai]], [[Emperor Ōjin]] and [[Empress Jingū]]. == 1.Origin & Religious significance == According to shrine legend, the shrine was founded as far back as the [[Jindai moji|Shin period]] (mythical age), or perhaps "Takachiho Palace, which was the palace of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ホオリ Amatsuhitaka Hiko Hohoemi] no Mikoto during the reign of [[Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jinmu]] (660-585 BC), was converted into a shrine. The shrine was relocated to its current location in [[708]], and a [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/摂社 regent shrine], Ishitai Shrine, is now located on the former site. Takayama Mausoleum, which is said to be the mausoleum of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ホオリ%20Amatsuhitaka%20Hiko%20Hohoemi Hohodemi no Mikoto], is located 13 km northwest of the shrine. It is said that the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/八幡神 Hachiman God] was manifested in [[544]] at this former shrine site. The reason why this shrine is called Sho-Hachiman is because the "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/八幡愚童訓 Hachiman Gudokun]'' says, "Ohiru-onna, the daughter of the great king of the Hinden Kingdom ([[China]] as seen from [[India]]), was seven years old when the light of the morning sun pierced her breast, and she became pregnant and gave birth to a prince. The king's retainers became suspicious, and put her on an empty ship, which they floated on the ocean, requesting that the place where the ship was attached be given to them as their domain. The ship eventually arrived at the shore of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大隅 Chinsei-Osumi] in Japan, and the prince was named Hachiman. It is said that this was during the reign of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/継体天皇 Emperor Tsugitai]." The story goes on to say, "The Taishi arrived at the shore of Osumi, Chinsei, in Japan. In the "Jinja Keiyo '' written by Munei Shirai, the character is described as "Chen Daioh," and his daughter's name is said to be Hachiman. The "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/今昔物語集 Konjaku Monogatari-shu]" also states that the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/八幡神 Hachiman deity] first appeared in [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大隅国 Osumi Province], then moved to [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/宇佐神宮 Usa], and finally left his mark on [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/石清水八幡宮 Ishi Kiyomizu]. As indicated by the character for "positive" in "Osumi Sho Hachiman," Kagoshima Shrine is said to be the root shrine of the Hachiman shrines. According to legend, there was once a dispute between Kokubu Hachiman and [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/宇佐神宮 Usa Hachiman] over which was the legitimate Hachiman, and [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/宇佐神宮 Usa Hachiman] secretly sent 15 (or even 14) messengers to burn Kokubu Hachiman. The emissaries were so startled and frightened that they fled to [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/溝辺町 Mizobe], where they were punished by the gods and fell one after another, numbering as many as 13. The local people then took pity on those who had died in a different land, and built mounds to comfort their souls at the places where they had fallen, and named them "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/十三塚原 Jusanzukabara]" (thirteen mounds). This [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/十三塚原 Jusanzukabara] is located in the northern part of the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国分平野 Kokubu Plain] in [[Kagoshima Prefecture]], and [[Kagoshima Airport]] and the Jusanzukabara Historic Site Park based on this legend are located in the northeastern part of the area. There are several other legends concerning the Usa Hachiman messenger that differ in content from the above. == 2.History == The first mention of the shrine in reliable historical records is in the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/延喜式神名帳 Engishiki Shinmeicho], compiled during the reign of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/醍醐天皇 Emperor Daigo] (885-930 AD), which lists it as an "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/桑原郡 Oōsumi Province] Kuwabara-gun Kakojima Shrine," making it the highest-ranking shrine in the so-called Southern Kyushu region of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/日向 Hyuga], [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大隅 Oōsumi], and [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/薩摩 Satsuma]. Because of its high status, the shrine has produced many powerful national figures, such as the Kuwabata and Saisyo clans, from its priesthood. During the [[Heian period]] (794-1185), [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/宇佐神宮 Usa Hachiman] invited the Hachiman Bekkyo shrine in Gosho, Kyushu, and the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/八幡神 Hachiman deity] was enshrined at the shrine. Since then, the shrine has also been called Sho-Hachimangu Shrine, Osumi Sho-Hachimangu Shrine, [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国府八幡宮 Kokubu Hachimangu Shrine], and so on. From the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/戦国時代_(日本) Warring States Period] to the [[Edo period|Edo Period]], the shrine was revered by the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/島津氏 Shimazu clan], a local [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大名 feudal lord]. In 1871, the shrine was upgraded to the status of a national medium-ranked shrine under the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/近代社格制度 modern shrine ranking system] of the Meiji government as "Kagoshima Shrine. In 1874, the shrine was declared a "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/神宮 Jingu]" (which are the shrines above all the Shinto shrines), and was listed as a "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/官幣中社 Kanno-Chusha]" under the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/近代社格制度 modern shrine ranking system] m, and in 1895, it was promoted to a "Kanno-Taisya" (Grand Shrine) under the government mintage system. After the war, it became an [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/別表神社 annexed shrine] of the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/神社本庁 Jinja Honcho]. On November 19, 2021, the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/文化審議会 National Council for Cultural Affairs] reported that the main shrine building, the hall of worship, the imperial messenger hall, and the main shrine building of the regent Shisho Shrine should be designated as [[重要文化財|Important Cultural Properties]]. On February 9, 2022, the following year, the shrine was officially designated as an Important Cultural Property through a public announcement in the official gazette. == 3.Precinct == Shaden (nationally designated important cultural property) = The shaden consists of three halls: the honden (the main hall), the heiden (hall of offerings), and the haiden (worship hall). Honden (main hall) =  Some deity dwells in the go-shintai and is then enshrined in the honden. Haiden (worship hall) = A place where people pray to deity. The entrance of Kagoshima Shrine Rice fields in the shrine Tanokami (Folk Cultual Properties of Kagoshima) = Tanokami protects the rice paddies and brings a bountiful rice harrest. Miroku temple ruins (National Historic Site) Ruins of Kuwahata clan (National Historic Site) = They are closely associated with Kagoshima Shrine. Shakutai  shrine (located inside Kagoshima Shrine) = It's near the shaden. people pray for safe childbirth there. Takachiho Temple monument = The monument built as the place where the metropolitan once stood. == 4.Rituals == The annual festivals held at Kagoshima Shrine are as follows Nanakusamatsuri (January 7) A Shinto ritual to offer rice gruel with seven herbs on the seventh day of the New Year to the gods to bring in the New Year. [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/初午祭_(鹿児島神宮) Hatsuumasai] (nearest Sunday to January 18 of the old calendar) The origin of the Hatsuuma sai is said to have been inspired by a dream that Shimazu Takahisa, then lord of Kagoshima in the Muromachi period (1336-1573), had while overseeing renovation work on the Kagoshima Shrine, while sleeping in the palace. Fujimatsuri (March 10 of the Old calendar) It's a festival of flowers Otauematsuri (May 5 of the Old calendar) The Otaue matsuri is an event held at temples, shrines, and imperial rice paddies. Reisai (August 15 of the Old calendar) Rei sai is the most important of the annual rituals held at shrines. Tanabata (July 7) It celebrates the meeting of the deities Orihime and Hikoboshi. Ohamaori sai ((Third Sunday in October)) The parade of about 350 people, including portable shrines, warriors, gunmen, priestesses, and children, is led by a masked Sarutahiko mikoshi (portable shrine) amidst the sounds of traditional Japanese music. == 5.Cutural treasures == Important cultural property (Registered by government) ・Kagoshima jingu 3bildings   - main shine and worship hall   - imperial messenger's palace   - four auxiliary shines Konito odoshi yoroi (yoroi=armer) including helme and Osode (Registered in 1953 March 31) - Dedication from Kabayama Yoshihisa who was chief retainer of Shimazu cran.    (registered in 1953 March 31) ・Iroiro odoshi doumaru including helmet and Osode (Artifact)   -  Dedication from Shimazu Takahisa in 1558.     (loged in [[Reimeikan, Kagoshima Prefectural Center for Historical Material|Reimeikan]])     (registered in 1953 March 31) ・Iroiro odoshi doumaru (=armer) including helmet and Osode (Artifact)   - Dedication from Shimazu Takahisa in 1558.    (lodged in Tokyo National Museum)    (registered in 1953 March 31) ・Japanese sword:No title wrought by Norishige    -  Although it had been lost since it was requisitioned by the occupation force in post-war,       the sword which the feature matched with this one was found in Australia in 2022.    (registered in 1918,April 8) Japanese sword:Mei toku san wrought by Sousyuzyu Akihiro  -  It was wrought in 1392. Dedication from Shimazu Nariakira who was the twenty seventh       head boss of Shimazu cran.  -  Although it had lost since it was requisitioned by the occupation force in post-war, it was       found in an auction and then Kagoshima jin-gu repurchased it in 2003.     (logged in Reimeikan)     (registered in 1927 April 25) ○Historic site ・Osumi syou hatimangu site and the former site of Syake    (in 2013 October 17) Cultural property designated by Kagoshima prefecture ・Tangible cultural property 　↳・Stone garden lantern which was symbol of reconstruction of Syougu  (Construction)        (registered in 2014 April 22) 　↳・Ceramics owned by Kagoshima-jingu(Aartifact) 　　- it was designated  as tangible cultural property designated by         Kirishima city.(in 2008 March 25)       - it was designated  as tangible cultural property designated by         Kagoshima prefecture.(in 2010 April 23) Document of Kagoshima-jingu (Ancient writing document)       - The letter of appointment for Syou hachimangu shinkan myubu syoku, edict from a         senior official of syou hatimangu syuin, The letter of appointment to Sakai         Tameharu for syo hatimangu miya syurizyo syoku         (registered in 1987 March 16) ・Tengible folk cultural property 　↳ ・Miyauti no ta no kami         (registered in 1968 March 29) Cultural property designated by Kirishima city ・Tangible cultural property 　↳・Tsuji no tuno no hosyoku shurine(building)       - it was formerly Benzaitendo surrounded by Shirasagi lake beside Mirokuin temple. It         was moved to the present site because of the abolition of Buddhism in　 　     Meiji(1868~1912).        (designated in 2005 July 6) 　↳・Statue of the Kagoshima-jingu four devas (historical referense) 　　- It was found in the site of the present Hayato historical folk museum.                 (lodged there) 　　  (designated in 1994 June 7) 　↳・Jingu old stamp(histric referense) 　　 (designated in 1995 July 3) ・Historic site ↳・Miyasaka shell mound   - it was found in Ura sando.     (designated in 1995 December 8) ・Intangible folk cultural property ↳・Horse of 18th day     (designated in 1987 March 31) == 6. The king's retainers became suspicious, and put her on an empty ship, which they floated on the ocean, requesting that the place where the ship was attached be given to them as their domain. The ship eventually arrived at the shore of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大隅 Chinsei-Osumi] in Japan, and the prince was named Hachiman. It is said that this was during the reign of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/継体天皇 Emperor Tsugitai]." The story goes on to say, "The Taishi arrived at the shore of Osumi, Chinsei, in Japan. In the "Jinja Keiyo '' written by Munei Shirai, the character is described as "Chen Daioh," and his daughter's name is said to be Hachiman. The "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/今昔物語集 Konjaku Monogatari-shu]" also states that the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/八幡神 Hachiman deity] first appeared in [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大隅国 Osumi Province], then moved to [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/宇佐神宮 Usa], and finally left his mark on [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/石清水八幡宮 Ishi Kiyomizu]. As indicated by the character for "positive" in "Osumi Sho Hachiman," Kagoshima Shrine is said to be the root shrine of the Hachiman shrines. The emissaries were so startled and frightened that they fled to [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/溝辺町 Mizobe], where they were punished by the gods and fell one after another, numbering as many as 13. The local people then took pity on those who had died in a different land, and built mounds to comfort their souls at the places where they had fallen, and named them "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/十三塚原 Jusanzukabara]" (thirteen mounds). This [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/十三塚原 Jusanzukabara] is located in the northern part of the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国分平野 Kokubu Plain] in [[Kagoshima Prefecture]], and [[Kagoshima Airport]] and the Jusanzukabara Historic Site Park based on this legend are located in the northeastern part of the area. There are several other legends concerning the Usa Hachiman messenger that differ in content from the above. == 2.History == The first mention of the shrine in reliable historical records is in the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/延喜式神名帳 Engishiki Shinmeicho], compiled during the reign of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/醍醐天皇 Emperor Daigo] (885-930 AD), which lists it as an "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/桑原郡 Oōsumi Province] Kuwabara-gun Kakojima Shrine," making it the highest-ranking shrine in the so-called Southern Kyushu region of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/日向 Hyuga], [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大隅 Oōsumi], and [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/薩摩 Satsuma]. Because of its high status, the shrine has produced many powerful national figures, such as the Kuwabata and Saisyo clans, from its priesthood. During the [[Heian period]] (794-1185), [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/宇佐神宮 Usa Hachiman] invited the Hachiman Bekkyo shrine in Gosho, Kyushu, and the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/八幡神 Hachiman deity] was enshrined at the shrine. Honden (main hall) =  Some deity dwells in the go-shintai and is then enshrined in the honden. Haiden (worship hall) = A place where people pray to deity. The entrance of Kagoshima Shrine Rice fields in the shrine Tanokami (Folk Cultual Properties of Kagoshima) = Tanokami protects the rice paddies and brings a bountiful rice harrest. Miroku temple ruins (National Historic Site) Ruins of Kuwahata clan (National Historic Site) = They are closely associated with Kagoshima Shrine. Shakutai  shrine (located inside Kagoshima Shrine) = It's near the shaden. people pray for safe childbirth there. Takachiho Temple monument = The monument built as the place where the metropolitan once stood. == 4.Rituals == The annual festivals held at Kagoshima Shrine are as follows Nanakusamatsuri (January 7) A Shinto ritual to offer rice gruel with seven herbs on the seventh day of the New Year to the gods to bring in the New Year. [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/初午祭_(鹿児島神宮) Hatsuumasai] (nearest Sunday to January 18 of the old calendar) The origin of the Hatsuuma sai is said to have been inspired by a dream that Shimazu Takahisa, then lord of Kagoshima in the Muromachi period (1336-1573), had while overseeing renovation work on the Kagoshima Shrine, while sleeping in the palace. Fujimatsuri (March 10 of the Old calendar) It's a festival of flowers Otauematsuri (May 5 of the Old calendar) The Otaue matsuri is an event held at temples, shrines, and imperial rice paddies. Reisai (August 15 of the Old calendar) Rei sai is the most important of the annual rituals held at shrines. Tanabata (July 7) It celebrates the meeting of the deities Orihime and Hikoboshi. Ohamaori sai ((Third Sunday in October)) The parade of about 350 people, including portable shrines, warriors, gunmen, priestesses, and children, is led by a masked Sarutahiko mikoshi (portable shrine) amidst the sounds of traditional Japanese music. == 5.Cutural treasures == Important cultural property (Registered by government) ・Kagoshima jingu 3bildings   - main shine and worship hall   - imperial messenger's palace   - four auxiliary shines Konito odoshi yoroi (yoroi=armer) including helme and Osode (Registered in 1953 March 31) - Dedication from Kabayama Yoshihisa who was chief retainer of Shimazu cran.    (registered in 1953 March 31) ・Iroiro odoshi doumaru including helmet and Osode (Artifact)   -  Dedication from Shimazu Takahisa in 1558.     (loged in [[Reimeikan, Kagoshima Prefectural Center for Historical Material|Reimeikan]])     (registered in 1953 March 31) ・Iroiro odoshi doumaru (=armer) including helmet and Osode (Artifact)   - Dedication from Shimazu Takahisa in 1558.    (lodged in Tokyo National Museum)    (registered in 1953 March 31) ・Japanese sword:No title wrought by Norishige    -  Although it had been lost since it was requisitioned by the occupation force in post-war,       the sword which the feature matched with this one was found in Australia in 2022.    (registered in 1918,April 8) Japanese sword:Mei toku san wrought by Sousyuzyu Akihiro  -  It was wrought in 1392. {{Expand Japanese|鹿児島神宮|date=November 2010}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Kagoshima-jingū
鹿児島神宮 | image = Kagoshimajingu Chokushiden.JPG | caption = | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{Coord|31.75340|130.73814|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Hoori]]
[[Toyotama-hime]]
[[Emperor Chūai]]
[[Emperor Ōjin]]
[[Empress Jingū]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 2496, Hayato-chō Uchi, [[Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]]
[[Kagoshima Prefecture|Kagoshima]] 899-5116 | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Kagoshima Shrine'''|鹿児島神宮|''Kagoshima-jingū''}} is a Shinto shrine located in [[Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]], [[Kagoshima prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is dedicated to [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Emperor Chūai]], [[Emperor Ōjin]] and [[Empress Jingū]]. == 1.Origin & Religious significance == According to shrine legend, the shrine was founded as far back as the [[Jindai moji|Shin period]] (mythical age), or perhaps "Takachiho Palace, which was the palace of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ホオリ Amatsuhitaka Hiko Hohoemi] no Mikoto during the reign of [[Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jinmu]] (660-585 BC), was converted into a shrine. The shrine was relocated to its current location in [[708]], and a [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/摂社 regent shrine], Ishitai Shrine, is now located on the former site. Takayama Mausoleum, which is said to be the mausoleum of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ホオリ%20Amatsuhitaka%20Hiko%20Hohoemi Hohodemi no Mikoto], is located 13 km northwest of the shrine. It is said that the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/八幡神 Hachiman God] was manifested in [[544]] at this former shrine site. The reason why this shrine is called Sho-Hachiman is because the "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/八幡愚童訓 Hachiman Gudokun]'' says, "Ohiru-onna, the daughter of the great king of the Hinden Kingdom ([[China]] as seen from [[India]]), was seven years old when the light of the morning sun pierced her breast, and she became pregnant and gave birth to a prince. The king's retainers became suspicious, and put her on an empty ship, which they floated on the ocean, requesting that the place where the ship was attached be given to them as their domain. The ship eventually arrived at the shore of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大隅 Chinsei-Osumi] in Japan, and the prince was named Hachiman. It is said that this was during the reign of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/継体天皇 Emperor Tsugitai]." The story goes on to say, "The Taishi arrived at the shore of Osumi, Chinsei, in Japan. In the "Jinja Keiyo '' written by Munei Shirai, the character is described as "Chen Daioh," and his daughter's name is said to be Hachiman. The "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/今昔物語集 Konjaku Monogatari-shu]" also states that the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/八幡神 Hachiman deity] first appeared in [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大隅国 Osumi Province], then moved to [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/宇佐神宮 Usa], and finally left his mark on [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/石清水八幡宮 Ishi Kiyomizu]. As indicated by the character for "positive" in "Osumi Sho Hachiman," Kagoshima Shrine is said to be the root shrine of the Hachiman shrines. According to legend, there was once a dispute between Kokubu Hachiman and [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/宇佐神宮 Usa Hachiman] over which was the legitimate Hachiman, and [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/宇佐神宮 Usa Hachiman] secretly sent 15 (or even 14) messengers to burn Kokubu Hachiman. The emissaries were so startled and frightened that they fled to [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/溝辺町 Mizobe], where they were punished by the gods and fell one after another, numbering as many as 13. The local people then took pity on those who had died in a different land, and built mounds to comfort their souls at the places where they had fallen, and named them "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/十三塚原 Jusanzukabara]" (thirteen mounds). This [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/十三塚原 Jusanzukabara] is located in the northern part of the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国分平野 Kokubu Plain] in [[Kagoshima Prefecture]], and [[Kagoshima Airport]] and the Jusanzukabara Historic Site Park based on this legend are located in the northeastern part of the area. There are several other legends concerning the Usa Hachiman messenger that differ in content from the above. == 2.History == The first mention of the shrine in reliable historical records is in the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/延喜式神名帳 Engishiki Shinmeicho], compiled during the reign of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/醍醐天皇 Emperor Daigo] (885-930 AD), which lists it as an "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/桑原郡 Oōsumi Province] Kuwabara-gun Kakojima Shrine," making it the highest-ranking shrine in the so-called Southern Kyushu region of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/日向 Hyuga], [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大隅 Oōsumi], and [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/薩摩 Satsuma]. Because of its high status, the shrine has produced many powerful national figures, such as the Kuwabata and Saisyo clans, from its priesthood. During the [[Heian period]] (794-1185), [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/宇佐神宮 Usa Hachiman] invited the Hachiman Bekkyo shrine in Gosho, Kyushu, and the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/八幡神 Hachiman deity] was enshrined at the shrine. Since then, the shrine has also been called Sho-Hachimangu Shrine, Osumi Sho-Hachimangu Shrine, [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国府八幡宮 Kokubu Hachimangu Shrine], and so on. From the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/戦国時代_(日本) Warring States Period] to the [[Edo period|Edo Period]], the shrine was revered by the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/島津氏 Shimazu clan], a local [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大名 feudal lord]. In 1871, the shrine was upgraded to the status of a national medium-ranked shrine under the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/近代社格制度 modern shrine ranking system] of the Meiji government as "Kagoshima Shrine. In 1874, the shrine was declared a "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/神宮 Jingu]" (which are the shrines above all the Shinto shrines), and was listed as a "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/官幣中社 Kanno-Chusha]" under the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/近代社格制度 modern shrine ranking system] m, and in 1895, it was promoted to a "Kanno-Taisya" (Grand Shrine) under the government mintage system. After the war, it became an [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/別表神社 annexed shrine] of the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/神社本庁 Jinja Honcho]. On November 19, 2021, the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/文化審議会 National Council for Cultural Affairs] reported that the main shrine building, the hall of worship, the imperial messenger hall, and the main shrine building of the regent Shisho Shrine should be designated as [[重要文化財|Important Cultural Properties]]. On February 9, 2022, the following year, the shrine was officially designated as an Important Cultural Property through a public announcement in the official gazette. == 3.Precinct == [[File:Kagoshima-jingu Decoration of Shrine Buildings 001.jpg|thumb|The decoration of the heiden (hall of offerings)]] [[File:Kagoshima-jingu Decoration of Shrine Buildings 002.jpg|thumb|The decoration of the haiden (worship hall)]] Shaden (nationally designated important cultural property) = The shaden consists of three halls: the honden (the main hall), the heiden (hall of offerings), and the haiden (worship hall). Honden (main hall) =  Some deity dwells in the go-shintai and is then enshrined in the honden. Haiden (worship hall) = A place where people pray to deity. The entrance of Kagoshima Shrine Rice fields in the shrine Tanokami (Folk Cultual Properties of Kagoshima) = Tanokami protects the rice paddies and brings a bountiful rice harrest. Miroku temple ruins (National Historic Site) Ruins of Kuwahata clan (National Historic Site) = They are closely associated with Kagoshima Shrine. Shakutai  shrine (located inside Kagoshima Shrine) = It's near the shaden. people pray for safe childbirth there. Takachiho Temple monument = The monument built as the place where the metropolitan once stood. == 4.Rituals == The annual festivals held at Kagoshima Shrine are as follows Nanakusamatsuri (January 7) A Shinto ritual to offer rice gruel with seven herbs on the seventh day of the New Year to the gods to bring in the New Year. [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/初午祭_(鹿児島神宮) Hatsuumasai] (nearest Sunday to January 18 of the old calendar) The origin of the Hatsuuma sai is said to have been inspired by a dream that Shimazu Takahisa, then lord of Kagoshima in the Muromachi period (1336-1573), had while overseeing renovation work on the Kagoshima Shrine, while sleeping in the palace. Fujimatsuri (March 10 of the Old calendar) It's a festival of flowers Otauematsuri (May 5 of the Old calendar) The Otaue matsuri is an event held at temples, shrines, and imperial rice paddies. Reisai (August 15 of the Old calendar) Rei sai is the most important of the annual rituals held at shrines. Tanabata (July 7) It celebrates the meeting of the deities Orihime and Hikoboshi. Ohamaori sai ((Third Sunday in October)) The parade of about 350 people, including portable shrines, warriors, gunmen, priestesses, and children, is led by a masked Sarutahiko mikoshi (portable shrine) amidst the sounds of traditional Japanese music. == 5.Cutural treasures == Important cultural property (Registered by government) ・Kagoshima jingu 3bildings   - main shine and worship hall   - imperial messenger's palace   - four auxiliary shines Konito odoshi yoroi (yoroi=armer) including helme and Osode (Registered in 1953 March 31) - Dedication from Kabayama Yoshihisa who was chief retainer of Shimazu cran.    (registered in 1953 March 31) ・Iroiro odoshi doumaru including helmet and Osode (Artifact)   -  Dedication from Shimazu Takahisa in 1558.     (loged in [[Reimeikan, Kagoshima Prefectural Center for Historical Material|Reimeikan]])     (registered in 1953 March 31) ・Iroiro odoshi doumaru (=armer) including helmet and Osode (Artifact)   - Dedication from Shimazu Takahisa in 1558.    (lodged in Tokyo National Museum)    (registered in 1953 March 31) ・Japanese sword:No title wrought by Norishige    -  Although it had been lost since it was requisitioned by the occupation force in post-war,       the sword which the feature matched with this one was found in Australia in 2022.    (registered in 1918,April 8) Japanese sword:Mei toku san wrought by Sousyuzyu Akihiro  -  It was wrought in 1392. Dedication from Shimazu Nariakira who was the twenty seventh       head boss of Shimazu cran.  -  Although it had lost since it was requisitioned by the occupation force in post-war, it was       found in an auction and then Kagoshima jin-gu repurchased it in 2003.     (logged in Reimeikan)     (registered in 1927 April 25) ○Historic site ・Osumi syou hatimangu site and the former site of Syake    (in 2013 October 17) Cultural property designated by Kagoshima prefecture ・Tangible cultural property 　↳・Stone garden lantern which was symbol of reconstruction of Syougu  (Construction)        (registered in 2014 April 22) 　↳・Ceramics owned by Kagoshima-jingu(Aartifact) 　　- it was designated  as tangible cultural property designated by         Kirishima city.(in 2008 March 25)       - it was designated  as tangible cultural property designated by         Kagoshima prefecture.(in 2010 April 23) Document of Kagoshima-jingu (Ancient writing document)       - The letter of appointment for Syou hachimangu shinkan myubu syoku, edict from a         senior official of syou hatimangu syuin, The letter of appointment to Sakai         Tameharu for syo hatimangu miya syurizyo syoku         (registered in 1987 March 16) ・Tengible folk cultural property 　↳ ・Miyauti no ta no kami         (registered in 1968 March 29) Cultural property designated by Kirishima city ・Tangible cultural property 　↳・Tsuji no tuno no hosyoku shurine(building)       - it was formerly Benzaitendo surrounded by Shirasagi lake beside Mirokuin temple. It         was moved to the present site because of the abolition of Buddhism in　 　     Meiji(1868~1912).        (designated in 2005 July 6) 　↳・Statue of the Kagoshima-jingu four devas (historical referense) 　　- It was found in the site of the present Hayato historical folk museum.                 (lodged there) 　　  (designated in 1994 June 7) 　↳・Jingu old stamp(histric referense) 　　 (designated in 1995 July 3) ・Historic site ↳・Miyasaka shell mound   - it was found in Ura sando.     (designated in 1995 December 8) ・Intangible folk cultural property ↳・Horse of 18th day     (designated in 1987 March 31) == 6. There are several other legends concerning the Usa Hachiman messenger that differ in content from the above. == 2.History == The first mention of the shrine in reliable historical records is in the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/延喜式神名帳 Engishiki Shinmeicho], compiled during the reign of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/醍醐天皇 Emperor Daigo] (885-930 AD), which lists it as an "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/桑原郡 Oōsumi Province] Kuwabara-gun Kakojima Shrine," making it the highest-ranking shrine in the so-called Southern Kyushu region of [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/日向 Hyuga], [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大隅 Oōsumi], and [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/薩摩 Satsuma]. Because of its high status, the shrine has produced many powerful national figures, such as the Kuwabata and Saisyo clans, from its priesthood. During the [[Heian period]] (794-1185), [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/宇佐神宮 Usa Hachiman] invited the Hachiman Bekkyo shrine in Gosho, Kyushu, and the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/八幡神 Hachiman deity] was enshrined at the shrine. Since then, the shrine has also been called Sho-Hachimangu Shrine, Osumi Sho-Hachimangu Shrine, [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/国府八幡宮 Kokubu Hachimangu Shrine], and so on. From the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/戦国時代_(日本) Warring States Period] to the [[Edo period|Edo Period]], the shrine was revered by the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/島津氏 Shimazu clan], a local [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/大名 feudal lord]. In 1871, the shrine was upgraded to the status of a national medium-ranked shrine under the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/近代社格制度 modern shrine ranking system] of the Meiji government as "Kagoshima Shrine. In 1874, the shrine was declared a "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/神宮 Jingu]" (which are the shrines above all the Shinto shrines), and was listed as a "[https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/官幣中社 Kanno-Chusha]" under the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/近代社格制度 modern shrine ranking system] m, and in 1895, it was promoted to a "Kanno-Taisya" (Grand Shrine) under the government mintage system. After the war, it became an [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/別表神社 annexed shrine] of the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/神社本庁 Jinja Honcho]. On November 19, 2021, the [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/文化審議会 National Council for Cultural Affairs] reported that the main shrine building, the hall of worship, the imperial messenger hall, and the main shrine building of the regent Shisho Shrine should be designated as [[重要文化財|Important Cultural Properties]]. On February 9, 2022, the following year, the shrine was officially designated as an Important Cultural Property through a public announcement in the official gazette. == 3.Precinct == [[File:Kagoshima-jingu Decoration of Shrine Buildings 001.jpg|thumb|The decoration of the heiden (hall of offerings)]] [[File:Kagoshima-jingu Decoration of Shrine Buildings 002.jpg|thumb|The decoration of the haiden (worship hall)]] Shaden (nationally designated important cultural property) = The shaden consists of three halls: the honden (the main hall), the heiden (hall of offerings), and the haiden (worship hall). Honden (main hall) =  Some deity dwells in the go-shintai and is then enshrined in the honden. Haiden (worship hall) = A place where people pray to deity. The entrance of Kagoshima Shrine Rice fields in the shrine Tanokami (Folk Cultual Properties of Kagoshima) = Tanokami protects the rice paddies and brings a bountiful rice harrest. Miroku temple ruins (National Historic Site) Ruins of Kuwahata clan (National Historic Site) = They are closely associated with Kagoshima Shrine. Shakutai  shrine (located inside Kagoshima Shrine) = It's near the shaden. people pray for safe childbirth there. Takachiho Temple monument = The monument built as the place where the metropolitan once stood. == 4.Rituals == The annual festivals held at Kagoshima Shrine are as follows Nanakusamatsuri (January 7) A Shinto ritual to offer rice gruel with seven herbs on the seventh day of the New Year to the gods to bring in the New Year. [https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/初午祭_(鹿児島神宮) Hatsuumasai] (nearest Sunday to January 18 of the old calendar) The origin of the Hatsuuma sai is said to have been inspired by a dream that Shimazu Takahisa, then lord of Kagoshima in the Muromachi period (1336-1573), had while overseeing renovation work on the Kagoshima Shrine, while sleeping in the palace. Fujimatsuri (March 10 of the Old calendar) It's a festival of flowers Otauematsuri (May 5 of the Old calendar) The Otaue matsuri is an event held at temples, shrines, and imperial rice paddies. Reisai (August 15 of the Old calendar) Rei sai is the most important of the annual rituals held at shrines. Tanabata (July 7) It celebrates the meeting of the deities Orihime and Hikoboshi. Ohamaori sai ((Third Sunday in October)) The parade of about 350 people, including portable shrines, warriors, gunmen, priestesses, and children, is led by a masked Sarutahiko mikoshi (portable shrine) amidst the sounds of traditional Japanese music. == 5.Cultural treasures == Important cultural property (Registered by government) ・Kagoshima jingu 3bildings   - main shine and worship hall   - imperial messenger's palace   - four auxiliary shines Konito odoshi yoroi (yoroi=armer) including helme and Osode (Registered in 1953 March 31) - Dedication from Kabayama Yoshihisa who was chief retainer of Shimazu cran.    (registered in 1953 March 31) ・Iroiro odoshi doumaru including helmet and Osode (Artifact)   -  Dedication from Shimazu Takahisa in 1558.     (loged in [[Reimeikan, Kagoshima Prefectural Center for Historical Material|Reimeikan]])     (registered in 1953 March 31) ・Iroiro odoshi doumaru (=armer) including helmet and Osode (Artifact)   - Dedication from Shimazu Takahisa in 1558.    (lodged in Tokyo National Museum)    (registered in 1953 March 31) ・Japanese sword:No title wrought by Norishige    -  Although it had been lost since it was requisitioned by the occupation force in post-war,       the sword which the feature matched with this one was found in Australia in 2022.    (registered in 1918,April 8) Japanese sword:Mei toku san wrought by Sousyuzyu Akihiro  -  It was wrought in 1392. Dedication from Shimazu Nariakira who was the twenty seventh       head boss of Shimazu cran.  -  Although it had lost since it was requisitioned by the occupation force in post-war, it was       found in an auction and then Kagoshima jin-gu repurchased it in 2003.     (logged in Reimeikan)     (registered in 1927 April 25) ○Historic site ・Osumi syou hatimangu site and the former site of Syake    (in 2013 October 17) Cultural property designated by Kagoshima prefecture ・Tangible cultural property 　↳・Stone garden lantern which was symbol of reconstruction of Syougu  (Construction)        (registered in 2014 April 22) 　↳・Ceramics owned by Kagoshima-jingu(Aartifact) 　　- it was designated  as tangible cultural property designated by         Kirishima city.(in 2008 March 25)       - it was designated  as tangible cultural property designated by         Kagoshima prefecture.(in 2010 April 23) Document of Kagoshima-jingu (Ancient writing document)       - The letter of appointment for Syou hachimangu shinkan myubu syoku, edict from a         senior official of syou hatimangu syuin, The letter of appointment to Sakai         Tameharu for syo hatimangu miya syurizyo syoku         (registered in 1987 March 16) ・Tengible folk cultural property 　↳ ・Miyauti no ta no kami         (registered in 1968 March 29) Cultural property designated by Kirishima city ・Tangible cultural property 　↳・Tsuji no tuno no hosyoku shurine(building)       - it was formerly Benzaitendo surrounded by Shirasagi lake beside Mirokuin temple. It         was moved to the present site because of the abolition of Buddhism in　 　     Meiji(1868~1912).        (designated in 2005 July 6) 　↳・Statue of the Kagoshima-jingu four devas (historical referense) 　　- It was found in the site of the present Hayato historical folk museum.                 (lodged there) 　　  (designated in 1994 June 7) 　↳・Jingu old stamp(histric referense) 　　 (designated in 1995 July 3) ・Historic site ↳・Miyasaka shell mound   - it was found in Ura sando.     (designated in 1995 December 8) ・Intangible folk cultural property ↳・Horse of 18th day     (designated in 1987 March 31) == 6. [[Kagoshima Prefecture|Kagoshima]] 899-5116 | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Kagoshima Shrine'''|鹿児島神宮|''Kagoshima-jingū''}} is a Shinto shrine located in [[Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]], [[Kagoshima prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is dedicated to [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Emperor Chūai]], [[Emperor Ōjin]] and [[Empress Jingū]]. == 1.Origin & Religious significance == According to shrine legend, the shrine was founded as far back as the [[Jindai moji|Shin period]] (mythical age), or perhaps "Takachiho Palace, which was the palace of [[:ja:ホオリ|Amatsuhitaka Hiko Hohoemi]] no Mikoto during the reign of [[Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jinmu]] (660-585 BC), was converted into a shrine. The shrine was relocated to its current location in [[708]], and a [[:ja:摂社|regent shrine]], Ishitai Shrine, is now located on the former site. Takayama Mausoleum, which is said to be the mausoleum of [[:ja:ホオリ Amatsuhitaka Hiko Hohoemi|Hohodemi no Mikoto]], is located 13 km northwest of the shrine. It is said that the [[:ja:八幡神|Hachiman God]] was manifested in [[544]] at this former shrine site. The reason why this shrine is called Sho-Hachiman is because the "[[:ja:八幡愚童訓|Hachiman Gudokun]]'' says, "Ohiru-onna, the daughter of the great king of the Hinden Kingdom ([[China]] as seen from [[India]]), was seven years old when the light of the morning sun pierced her breast, and she became pregnant and gave birth to a prince. The king's retainers became suspicious, and put her on an empty ship, which they floated on the ocean, requesting that the place where the ship was attached be given to them as their domain. The ship eventually arrived at the shore of [[:ja:大隅|Chinsei-Osumi]] in Japan, and the prince was named Hachiman. It is said that this was during the reign of [[:ja:継体天皇|Emperor Tsugitai]]." The story goes on to say, "The Taishi arrived at the shore of Osumi, Chinsei, in Japan. In the "Jinja Keiyo '' written by Munei Shirai, the character is described as "Chen Daioh," and his daughter's name is said to be Hachiman. The "[[:ja:今昔物語集|Konjaku Monogatari-shu]]" also states that the [[:ja:八幡神|Hachiman deity]] first appeared in [[:ja:大隅国|Osumi Province]], then moved to [[:ja:宇佐神宮|Usa]], and finally left his mark on [[:ja:石清水八幡宮|Ishi Kiyomizu]]. As indicated by the character for "positive" in "Osumi Sho Hachiman," Kagoshima Shrine is said to be the root shrine of the Hachiman shrines. According to legend, there was once a dispute between Kokubu Hachiman and [[:ja:宇佐神宮|Usa Hachiman]] over which was the legitimate Hachiman, and [[:ja:宇佐神宮|Usa Hachiman]] secretly sent 15 (or even 14) messengers to burn Kokubu Hachiman. The emissaries were so startled and frightened that they fled to [[:ja:溝辺町|Mizobe]], where they were punished by the gods and fell one after another, numbering as many as 13. The local people then took pity on those who had died in a different land, and built mounds to comfort their souls at the places where they had fallen, and named them "[[:ja:十三塚原|Jusanzukabara]]" (thirteen mounds). This [[:ja:十三塚原|Jusanzukabara]] is located in the northern part of the [[:ja:国分平野|Kokubu Plain]] in [[Kagoshima Prefecture]], and [[Kagoshima Airport]] and the Jusanzukabara Historic Site Park based on this legend are located in the northeastern part of the area. There are several other legends concerning the Usa Hachiman messenger that differ in content from the above. == 2.History == The first mention of the shrine in reliable historical records is in the [[:ja:延喜式神名帳|Engishiki Shinmeicho]], compiled during the reign of [[:ja:醍醐天皇|Emperor Daigo]] (885-930 AD), which lists it as an "[[:ja:桑原郡|Oōsumi Province]] Kuwabara-gun Kakojima Shrine," making it the highest-ranking shrine in the so-called Southern Kyushu region of [[:ja:日向|Hyuga]], [[:ja:大隅|Oōsumi]], and [[:ja:薩摩|Satsuma]]. Because of its high status, the shrine has produced many powerful national figures, such as the Kuwabata and Saisyo clans, from its priesthood. During the [[Heian period]] (794-1185), [[:ja:宇佐神宮|Usa Hachiman]] invited the Hachiman Bekkyo shrine in Gosho, Kyushu, and the [[:ja:八幡神|Hachiman deity]] was enshrined at the shrine. Since then, the shrine has also been called Sho-Hachimangu Shrine, Osumi Sho-Hachimangu Shrine, [[:ja:国府八幡宮|Kokubu Hachimangu Shrine]], and so on. From the [[:ja:戦国時代 (日本)|Warring States Period]] to the [[Edo period|Edo Period]], the shrine was revered by the [[:ja:島津氏|Shimazu clan]], a local [[:ja:大名|feudal lord]]. After the war, it became an [[:ja:別表神社|annexed shrine]] of the [[:ja:神社本庁|Jinja Honcho]]. [[Emperor Chūai]]

[[Empress Jingū]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 2496, Hayato-chō Uchi, [[Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]]
[[Kagoshima Prefecture|Kagoshima]] 899-5116 | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Kagoshima Shrine'''|鹿児島神宮|''Kagoshima-jingū''}} is a Shinto shrine located in [[Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]], [[Kagoshima prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is dedicated to [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Emperor Chūai]], [[Emperor Ōjin]] and [[Empress Jingū]]. == Origin & Religious significance == According to shrine legend, the shrine was founded as far back as the [[Jindai moji|Shin period]] (mythical age), or perhaps "Takachiho Palace, which was the palace of [[:ja:ホオリ|Amatsuhitaka Hiko Hohoemi]] no Mikoto during the reign of [[Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jinmu]] (660-585 BC), was converted into a shrine. The shrine was relocated to its current location in [[708]], and a [[:ja:摂社|regent shrine]], Ishitai Shrine, is now located on the former site. Takayama Mausoleum, which is said to be the mausoleum of [[:ja:ホオリ Amatsuhitaka Hiko Hohoemi|Hohodemi no Mikoto]], is located 13 km northwest of the shrine. It is said that the [[:ja:八幡神|Hachiman God]] was manifested in [[544]] at this former shrine site. The reason why this shrine is called Sho-Hachiman is because the "[[:ja:八幡愚童訓|Hachiman Gudokun]]'' says, "Ohiru-onna, the daughter of the great king of the Hinden Kingdom ([[China]] as seen from [[India]]), was seven years old when the light of the morning sun pierced her breast, and she became pregnant and gave birth to a prince. The king's retainers became suspicious, and put her on an empty ship, which they floated on the ocean, requesting that the place where the ship was attached be given to them as their domain. The ship eventually arrived at the shore of [[:ja:大隅|Chinsei-Osumi]] in Japan, and the prince was named Hachiman. It is said that this was during the reign of [[:ja:継体天皇|Emperor Tsugitai]]." The story goes on to say, "The Taishi arrived at the shore of Osumi, Chinsei, in Japan. In the "Jinja Keiyo '' written by Munei Shirai, the character is described as "Chen Daioh," and his daughter's name is said to be Hachiman. The "[[:ja:今昔物語集|Konjaku Monogatari-shu]]" also states that the [[:ja:八幡神|Hachiman deity]] first appeared in [[:ja:大隅国|Osumi Province]], then moved to [[:ja:宇佐神宮|Usa]], and finally left his mark on [[:ja:石清水八幡宮|Ishi Kiyomizu]]. As indicated by the character for "positive" in "Osumi Sho Hachiman," Kagoshima Shrine is said to be the root shrine of the Hachiman shrines. According to legend, there was once a dispute between Kokubu Hachiman and [[:ja:宇佐神宮|Usa Hachiman]] over which was the legitimate Hachiman, and [[:ja:宇佐神宮|Usa Hachiman]] secretly sent 15 (or even 14) messengers to burn Kokubu Hachiman. The emissaries were so startled and frightened that they fled to [[:ja:溝辺町|Mizobe]], where they were punished by the gods and fell one after another, numbering as many as 13. The local people then took pity on those who had died in a different land, and built mounds to comfort their souls at the places where they had fallen, and named them "[[:ja:十三塚原|Jusanzukabara]]" (thirteen mounds). This [[:ja:十三塚原|Jusanzukabara]] is located in the northern part of the [[:ja:国分平野|Kokubu Plain]] in [[Kagoshima Prefecture]], and [[Kagoshima Airport]] and the Jusanzukabara Historic Site Park based on this legend are located in the northeastern part of the area. There are several other legends concerning the Usa Hachiman messenger that differ in content from the above. == History == The first mention of the shrine in reliable historical records is in the [[Engishiki|Engishiki Shinmeicho]], compiled during the reign of [[Emperor Daigo]] (885-930 AD), which lists it as an "[[:ja:桑原郡|Oōsumi Province]] Kuwabara-gun Kakojima Shrine," making it the highest-ranking shrine in the so-called Southern Kyushu region of [[:ja:日向|Hyuga]], [[:ja:大隅|Oōsumi]], and [[:ja:薩摩|Satsuma]]. Because of its high status, the shrine has produced many powerful national figures, such as the Kuwabata and Saisyo clans, from its priesthood. During the [[Heian period]] (794-1185), [[:ja:宇佐神宮|Usa Hachiman]] invited the Hachiman Bekkyo shrine in Gosho, Kyushu, and the [[:ja:八幡神|Hachiman deity]] was enshrined at the shrine. Since then, the shrine has also been called Sho-Hachimangu Shrine, Osumi Sho-Hachimangu Shrine, [[:ja:国府八幡宮|Kokubu Hachimangu Shrine]], and so on. From the [[:ja:戦国時代 (日本)|Warring States Period]] to the [[Edo period|Edo Period]], the shrine was revered by the [[:ja:島津氏|Shimazu clan]], a local [[:ja:大名|feudal lord]]. In 1871, the shrine was upgraded to the status of a national medium-ranked shrine under the [[:ja:近代社格制度|modern shrine ranking system]] of the Meiji government as "Kagoshima Shrine. In 1874, the shrine was declared a "[[:ja:神宮|Jingu]]" (which are the shrines above all the Shinto shrines), and was listed as a "[[:ja:官幣中社|Kanno-Chusha]]" under the [[:ja:近代社格制度|modern shrine ranking system]] m, and in 1895, it was promoted to a "Kanno-Taisya" (Grand Shrine) under the government mintage system. After the war, it became an [[Beppyo shrine|annexed shrine]] of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines|Jinja Honcho]]. On November 19, 2021, the [[:ja:文化審議会|National Council for Cultural Affairs]] reported that the main shrine building, the hall of worship, the imperial messenger hall, and the main shrine building of the regent Shisho Shrine should be designated as [[重要文化財|Important Cultural Properties]]. On February 9, 2022, the following year, the shrine was officially designated as an Important Cultural Property through a public announcement in the official gazette. == Precinct == [[File:Kagoshima-jingu Decoration of Shrine Buildings 001.jpg|thumb|The decoration of the heiden (hall of offerings)]] [[File:Kagoshima-jingu Decoration of Shrine Buildings 002.jpg|thumb|The decoration of the haiden (worship hall)]] Shaden (nationally designated important cultural property) = The shaden consists of three halls: the honden (the main hall), the heiden (hall of offerings), and the haiden (worship hall). Honden (main hall) = Some deity dwells in the go-shintai and is then enshrined in the honden. Haiden (worship hall) = A place where people pray to deity. The entrance of Kagoshima Shrine Rice fields in the shrine Tanokami (Folk Cultual Properties of Kagoshima) = Tanokami protects the rice paddies and brings a bountiful rice harrest. Miroku temple ruins (National Historic Site) Ruins of Kuwahata clan (National Historic Site) = They are closely associated with Kagoshima Shrine. Shakutai shrine (located inside Kagoshima Shrine) = It's near the shaden. people pray for safe childbirth there. Takachiho Temple monument = The monument built as the place where the metropolitan once stood. == Rituals == The annual festivals held at Kagoshima Shrine are as follows Nanakusamatsuri (January 7) A Shinto ritual to offer rice gruel with seven herbs on the seventh day of the New Year to the gods to bring in the New Year. [[:ja:初午祭 (鹿児島神宮)|Hatsuumasai]] (nearest Sunday to January 18 of the old calendar) The origin of the Hatsuuma sai is said to have been inspired by a dream that Shimazu Takahisa, then lord of Kagoshima in the Muromachi period (1336-1573), had while overseeing renovation work on the Kagoshima Shrine, while sleeping in the palace. Fujimatsuri (March 10 of the Old calendar) It's a festival of flowers Otauematsuri (May 5 of the Old calendar) The Otaue matsuri is an event held at temples, shrines, and imperial rice paddies. Reisai (August 15 of the Old calendar) Rei sai is the most important of the annual rituals held at shrines. Tanabata (July 7) It celebrates the meeting of the deities Orihime and Hikoboshi. Ohamaori sai ((Third Sunday in October)) The parade of about 350 people, including portable shrines, warriors, gunmen, priestesses, and children, is led by a masked Sarutahiko mikoshi (portable shrine) amidst the sounds of traditional Japanese music. == Cultural treasures == Important cultural property (Registered by government) ・Kagoshima jingu 3bildings - main shine and worship hall - imperial messenger's palace - four auxiliary shines Konito odoshi yoroi (yoroi=armer) including helme and Osode (Registered in 1953 March 31) - Dedication from Kabayama Yoshihisa who was chief retainer of Shimazu cran. Dedication from Shimazu Nariakira who was the twenty seventh head boss of Shimazu cran. - Although it had lost since it was requisitioned by the occupation force in post-war, it was found in an auction and then Kagoshima jin-gu repurchased it in 2003. Historically it was also known by the names "Osumi Sho Hachimangu" and "Kokubu Hachimangu". == Enshrined ''Kami'' == The kami enshrined are as follows:{{Cite web |title=由緒について - 鹿児島神宮 |url=https://kagoshima-jingu.jp/yuisyo.php |access-date=2022-09-28 |website=kagoshima-jingu.jp}} ; Main shrine * Hoori: Amatsuhidakahiko Hohodemi no Mikoto (天津日高彦火火出見尊) * Toyotama-hime (豊玉比売命''')''' ; Subsidiary shrines * Emperor Chuai (帯中比子尊) * Empress Jingu (息長帯比売命) - Wife of Emperor Chuai. * Emperor Ojin (品陀和気尊) * Empress Nakatsu (中比売命) - Wife of Emperor Ojin. == History == According to legend, the shrine was founded during the [[Age of the Gods]], as Takachiho Palace, the palace of Hoori, during the reign of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. The shrine was relocated to its current location in 708. Sekitai Shrine is located on the former site. Takayanoyamano [[Mausoleum|Mausoleum,]] said to be the mausoleum of Hoori, is located 13 km northwest of the shrine. It is said that the God [[Hachiman]] was born in 544 at the former shrine site. This is the reason why the shrine was called Sho-Hachiman. According to legend, "Ohirume, the daughter of a great [[India|Indian]] king, was seven years old when the light of the morning sun pierced her breast. She conceived and gave [[Virgin birth (mythology)|birth]] to a prince. The king's retainers became suspicious, and put her on an empty ship, which they floated on the ocean, requesting that the place where the ship landed be given to them as their domain. The ship eventually arrived at the shore of [[Chinzei, Saga|Chinzei]], Osumi in Japan, and the prince was named Hachiman. It is said that this was during the reign of [[Emperor Keitai]]. " The story goes on to say, "The prince arrived at the shore of Chinzei, Osumi in Japan. In "the Jinja Keiyo" written by Munei Shirai, the Indian king is named "Great King Chen," and his daughter's name is also said to be Hachiman.{{Cite web |title=神社啓蒙 7巻目録1巻. [5] - 国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/2556086 |access-date=2022-09-28 |website=dl.ndl.go.jp |language=ja}} It is written in the [[Konjaku Monogatarishū|Konjaku Monogatarishu]] that Hachiman first appeared in Osumi Province, then moved to [[Usa, Ōita|Usa]], before finally leaving his mark at the Ishimizu shrine. ==External links== {{Commons category|Kagoshima-jingu|Kagoshima Shrine}} * {{OSM|n|4459864389}} {{Shinto shrine}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kagoshima Prefecture]] [[Category:Kanpei-taisha]]

The shrine was relocated to its current location in 708. Sekitai Shrine is located on the original site. Takayanoyamano [[Mausoleum]], said to be the mausoleum of Hoori, is located 13 km northwest of the shrine. It is said that the God [[Hachiman]] was born in 544 at the former shrine site. This is the reason why the shrine was called Sho-Hachiman. According to legend, "Ohirume, the daughter of a great king of [[Chinas]], was seven years old when the light of the morning sun pierced her breast. She conceived and gave [[Virgin birth (mythology)|birth]] to a prince. The king's retainers became suspicious, and put her on an empty ship, which they floated on the ocean, requesting that the place where the ship landed be given to them as their domain. The ship eventually arrived at the shore of [[Chinzei]], Osumi in Japan, and the prince was named Hachiman. It is said that this was during the reign of [[Emperor Keitai]]. " The story goes on to say, "The prince arrived at the shore of Chinzei, Osumi in Japan. In "the Jinja Keiyo" written by Munei Shirai, the king is named "Great King Chen," and his daughter's name is also said to be named Hachiman.{{Cite web |title=神社啓蒙 7巻目録1巻. The local people then took pity on those who had died in a different land, and built mounds to comfort their souls at the places where they had fallen. These mounds are located in the northern part of the Kokubu Plain in Kagoshima Prefecture. The Jusanzukabara (Thirteen Mounds) Historic Site Park derives its name from this legend legend is located in the northeastern part of the area, near [[Kagoshima Airport]]. There are several other legends concerning the messenger of Usa Hachiman that differ in content from the above. There are several other legends concerning the Usa Hachiman emissary that differ in content from the above. The first mention of the shrine in reliable historical records is in the Engishiki, compiled during the reign of [[Emperor Daigo]], which lists it as an "Osumi Province Kuwabara-gun Kagoshima Shrine," making it the highest-ranking shrine in the called Southern Kyushu region of Hyuga, Osumi, and Satsuma. Because of its high prestige, the shrine produced a number of prominent priests from the Kuwabata and Saisho clans. It is said that the God Hachiman himself was enshrined here during the Heian period (794-1185), when Usa Hachiman shrine invited the Hachiman Betsugu shrine of the Kyushu Gosho to go to Kagoshima Shrine. Since then, the shrine has also been called Sho-Hachimangu, Osumi Sho-Hachimangu, and Kokubu Hachimangu. One of the 2,861 shrines listed in the [[Engishiki]], it is the first shrine in the historic [[Ōsumi Province|Osumi Province]]. It is dedicated to [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Emperor Chūai]], [[Emperor Ōjin]] and [[Empress Jingū]]. It is classified as a Beppyo shrine, according to the Association of Shinto Shrines. Historically it was also known by the names "Osumi Sho Hachimangu" and "Kokubu Hachimangu". == Enshrined ''Kami'' == The kami enshrined are as follows:{{Cite web |title=由緒について - 鹿児島神宮 |url=https://kagoshima-jingu.jp/yuisyo.php |access-date=2022-09-28 |website=kagoshima-jingu.jp}} ; Main shrine * Hoori: Amatsuhidakahiko Hohodemi no Mikoto (天津日高彦火火出見尊) * Toyotama-hime (豊玉比売命''')''' ; Subsidiary shrines * Emperor Chuai (帯中比子尊) * Empress Jingu (息長帯比売命) - Wife of Emperor Chuai. * Emperor Ojin (品陀和気尊) * Empress Nakatsu (中比売命) - Wife of Emperor Ojin. == History == According to legend, the shrine was founded during the [[Age of the Gods]], as Takachiho Palace, the residence of Hoori, during the reign of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. This is the reason why the shrine was called Sho-Hachiman. According to legend, "Ohirume, the daughter of a great king of [[Chinas]], was seven years old when the light of the morning sun pierced her breast. She conceived and gave [[Virgin birth (mythology)|birth]] to a prince. The king's retainers became suspicious, and put her on an empty ship, which they floated on the ocean, requesting that the place where the ship landed be given to them as their domain. The ship eventually arrived at the shore of [[Chinzei]], Osumi in Japan, and the prince was named Hachiman. It is said that this was during the reign of [[Emperor Keitai]]. " The story goes on to say, "The prince arrived at the shore of Chinzei, Osumi in Japan. In "the Jinja Keiyo" written by Munei Shirai, the king is named "Great King Chen," and his daughter's name is also said to be named Hachiman.{{Cite web |title=神社啓蒙 7巻目録1巻. The local people then took pity on those who had died in a different land, and built mounds to comfort their souls at the places where they had fallen. From the Sengoku Period to the Edo Period, the shrine was patronized by the [[Shimazu clan]]. In 1871, the shrine was given a higher ranking under the Meiji government's modern shrine ranking system under the name "Kagoshima Shrine". This happened again in 1874, and once more in 1895 when it was promoted to a Grand Shrine. After the war, the shrine became a part of the Association of Shinto Shrines. On November 19, 2021, the National Council for Cultural Affairs reported that the main shrine, the hall of worship, the imperial messenger hall, and the main shrine would be designated as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]. The following year, February 9, 2022, this was reported in the official gazette and they were officially designated as Important Cultural Properties.{{Cite web |last=霧島市 |title=国宝・重要文化財(建造物)の指定について |url=http://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kokuhoukettei.html |access-date=2022-09-29 |website=霧島市 |language=ja}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons category|Kagoshima-jingu|Kagoshima Shrine}} * {{OSM|n|4459864389}} {{Shinto shrine}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kagoshima Prefecture]] [[Category:Kanpei-taisha]]

[[Kagoshima Prefecture|Kagoshima]] 899-5116 | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Kagoshima Shrine'''|鹿児島神宮|''Kagoshima-jingū''}} is a Shinto shrine located in [[Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]], [[Kagoshima prefecture]], [[Japan]]. One of the 2,861 shrines listed in the [[Engishiki]], it is the first shrine in the historic [[Ōsumi Province|Osumi Province]]. It is dedicated to [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Emperor Chūai]], [[Emperor Ōjin]] and [[Empress Jingū]]. It is classified as a Beppyo shrine, according to the Association of Shinto Shrines. Historically it was also known by the names "Osumi Sho Hachimangu" and "Kokubu Hachimangu". == Enshrined ''Kami'' == The kami enshrined are as follows:{{Cite web |title=由緒について - 鹿児島神宮 |url=https://kagoshima-jingu.jp/yuisyo.php |access-date=2022-09-28 |website=kagoshima-jingu.jp}} ; Main shrine * Hoori: Amatsuhidakahiko Hohodemi no Mikoto (天津日高彦火火出見尊) * Toyotama-hime (豊玉比売命''')''' ; Subsidiary shrines * Emperor Chuai (帯中比子尊) * Empress Jingu (息長帯比売命) - Wife of Emperor Chuai. * Emperor Ojin (品陀和気尊) * Empress Nakatsu (中比売命) - Wife of Emperor Ojin. == History == According to legend, the shrine was founded during the [[Age of the Gods]], as Takachiho Palace, the residence of Hoori, during the reign of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. The shrine was relocated to its current location in 708. Sekitai Shrine is located on the original site. Takayanoyamano [[Mausoleum]], said to be the mausoleum of Hoori, is located 13 km northwest of the shrine. It is said that the God [[Hachiman]] was born in 544 at the former shrine site. This is the reason why the shrine was called Sho-Hachiman. According to legend, "Ohirume, the daughter of a great king of [[Chinas]], was seven years old when the light of the morning sun pierced her breast. She conceived and gave [[Virgin birth (mythology)|birth]] to a prince. The king's retainers became suspicious, and put her on an empty ship, which they floated on the ocean, requesting that the place where the ship landed be given to them as their domain. The ship eventually arrived at the shore of [[Chinzei]], Osumi in Japan, and the prince was named Hachiman. It is said that this was during the reign of [[Emperor Keitai]]. " The story goes on to say, "The prince arrived at the shore of Chinzei, Osumi in Japan. In "the Jinja Keiyo" written by Munei Shirai, the king is named "Great King Chen," and his daughter's name is also said to be named Hachiman.{{Cite web |title=神社啓蒙 7巻目録1巻. [5] - 国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/2556086 |access-date=2022-09-28 |website=dl.ndl.go.jp |language=ja}} It is written in the [[Konjaku Monogatarishū|Konjaku Monogatarishu]] that Hachiman first appeared in Osumi Province, then moved to [[Usa, Ōita|Usa]], before finally leaving his mark at the Ishimizu shrine. As the Chinese character for "Correct (正)" indicates, Kagoshima Shrine is said to be the most legitimate Hachiman Shrine. According to legend, there was once a dispute between Kagoshima Hachiman shrine (At the time known as Kokubu Hachiman shrine) and Usa Hachiman shrine over which was the more legitimate Hachiman shrine. Usa Hachiman shrine secretly sent 15 (or even 14) messengers to burn down Kagoshima Hachiman shrine. As that happened, the character for "Shohachiman (正八幡)" appeared in the black smoke rising from the burning shrine. These messengers were so frightened that they fled to [[Mizobe, Kagoshima|Mizobe]], where they were punished by the gods and 13 died one after another. The local people then took pity on those who had died in a different land, and built mounds to comfort their souls at the places where they had fallen. These mounds are located in the northern part of the Kokubu Plain in Kagoshima Prefecture. The Jusanzukabara (Thirteen Mounds) Historic Site Park derives its name from this legend legend is located in the northeastern part of the area, near [[Kagoshima Airport]]. There are several other legends concerning the messenger of Usa Hachiman that differ in content from the above. There are several other legends concerning the Usa Hachiman emissary that differ in content from the above. The first mention of the shrine in reliable historical records is in the Engishiki, compiled during the reign of [[Emperor Daigo]], which lists it as an "Osumi Province Kuwabara-gun Kagoshima Shrine," making it the highest-ranking shrine in the called Southern Kyushu region of Hyuga, Osumi, and Satsuma. Because of its high prestige, the shrine produced a number of prominent priests from the Kuwabata and Saisho clans. It is said that the God Hachiman himself was enshrined here during the Heian period (794-1185), when Usa Hachiman shrine invited the Hachiman Betsugu shrine of the Kyushu Gosho to go to Kagoshima Shrine. Since then, the shrine has also been called Sho-Hachimangu, Osumi Sho-Hachimangu, and Kokubu Hachimangu. During the [[Kenkyū|Kenkyu period]] (1190 - 1199), the shrine's territory was over 2,500 town hectares, and it held 1,000 [[koku]] until the end of the [[Edo period]].{{Cite web |title=鹿児島神宮 {{!}} 鹿児島県神社庁 |url=https://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/tanbou/28/ |access-date=2022-09-29 |website=www.kagojinjacho.or.jp}} From the Sengoku Period to the Edo Period, the shrine was patronized by the [[Shimazu clan]]. In 1871, the shrine was given a higher ranking under the Meiji government's modern shrine ranking system under the name "Kagoshima Shrine". This happened again in 1874, and once more in 1895 when it was promoted to a Grand Shrine. After the war, the shrine became a part of the Association of Shinto Shrines. On November 19, 2021, the National Council for Cultural Affairs reported that the main shrine, the hall of worship, the imperial messenger hall, and the main shrine would be designated as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]. The following year, February 9, 2022, this was reported in the official gazette and they were officially designated as Important Cultural Properties.{{Cite web |last=霧島市 |title=国宝・重要文化財(建造物)の指定について |url=http://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kokuhoukettei.html |access-date=2022-09-29 |website=霧島市 |language=ja}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons category|Kagoshima-jingu|Kagoshima Shrine}} * {{OSM|n|4459864389}} {{Shinto shrine}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kagoshima Prefecture]] [[Category:Kanpei Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai Taisha]]

These messengers were so frightened that they fled to [[Mizobe, Kagoshima|Mizobe]], where they were punished by the gods and 13 died one after another. The local people then took pity on those who had died in a different land, and built mounds to comfort their souls at the places where they had fallen. These mounds are located in the northern part of the Kokubu Plain in Kagoshima Prefecture. The Jusanzukabara (Thirteen Mounds) Historic Site Park derives its name from this legend legend is located in the northeastern part of the area, near [[Kagoshima Airport]]. There are several other legends concerning the messenger of Usa Hachiman that differ in content from the above. There are several other legends concerning the Usa Hachiman emissary that differ in content from the above. The first mention of the shrine in reliable historical records is in the Engishiki, compiled during the reign of [[Emperor Daigo]], which lists it as an "Osumi Province Kuwabara-gun Kagoshima Shrine," making it the highest-ranking shrine in the called Southern Kyushu region of Hyuga, Osumi, and Satsuma. Because of its high prestige, the shrine produced a number of prominent priests from the Kuwabata and Saisho clans. It is said that the God Hachiman himself was enshrined here during the Heian period (794-1185), when Usa Hachiman shrine invited the Hachiman Betsugu shrine of the Kyushu Gosho to go to Kagoshima Shrine. Since then, the shrine has also been called Sho-Hachimangu, Osumi Sho-Hachimangu, and Kokubu Hachimangu. During the [[Kenkyū|Kenkyu period]] (1190 - 1199), the shrine's territory was over 2,500 town hectares, and it held 1,000 [[koku]] until the end of the [[Edo period]].{{Cite web |title=鹿児島神宮 {{!}} 鹿児島県神社庁 |url=https://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/tanbou/28/ |access-date=2022-09-29 |website=www.kagojinjacho.or.jp}} From the Sengoku Period to the Edo Period, the shrine was patronized by the [[Shimazu clan]]. In 1871, the shrine was given a higher ranking under the Meiji government's modern shrine ranking system under the name "Kagoshima Shrine". This happened again in 1874, and once more in 1895 when it was promoted to a Grand Shrine. After the war, the shrine became a part of the Association of Shinto Shrines. On November 19, 2021, the National Council for Cultural Affairs reported that the main shrine, the hall of worship, the imperial messenger hall, and the main shrine would be designated as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]]. The following year, February 9, 2022, this was reported in the official gazette and they were officially designated as Important Cultural Properties.{{Cite web |last=霧島市 |title=国宝・重要文化財(建造物)の指定について |url=http://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kokuhoukettei.html |access-date=2022-09-29 |website=霧島市 |language=ja}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons category|Kagoshima-jingu|Kagoshima Shrine}} * {{OSM|n|4459864389}} {{Shinto shrine}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kagoshima Prefecture]] [[Category:Kanpei Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai Taisha]] [[Category:Kagoshima Prefecture Important Cultural Properties]]

Historically it was also known by the names "Osumi Sho Hachimangu" and "Kokubu Hachimangu". == Enshrined ''Kami'' == The kami enshrined are as follows:{{Cite web |title=由緒について - 鹿児島神宮 |url=https://kagoshima-jingu.jp/yuisyo.php |access-date=2022-09-28 |website=kagoshima-jingu.jp}} ; Main shrine * Hoori: Amatsuhidakahiko Hohodemi no Mikoto (天津日高彦火火出見尊) * Toyotama-hime (豊玉比売命''')''' ; Subsidiary shrines * Emperor Chuai (帯中比子尊) * Empress Jingu (息長帯比売命) - Wife of Emperor Chuai. * Emperor Ojin (品陀和気尊) * Empress Nakatsu (中比売命) - Wife of Emperor Ojin. == History == According to legend, the shrine was founded during the [[Age of the Gods]], as Takachiho Palace, the residence of Hoori, during the reign of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. This is the reason why the shrine was called Sho-Hachiman. According to legend, "Ohirume, the daughter of a great king of [[Chinas]], was seven years old when the light of the morning sun pierced her breast. She conceived and gave [[Virgin birth (mythology)|birth]] to a prince. The king's retainers became suspicious, and put her on an empty ship, which they floated on the ocean, requesting that the place where the ship landed be given to them as their domain. The ship eventually arrived at the shore of [[Chinzei]], Osumi in Japan, and the prince was named Hachiman. It is said that this was during the reign of [[Emperor Keitai]]. " The story goes on to say, "The prince arrived at the shore of Chinzei, Osumi in Japan. In "the Jinja Keiyo" written by Munei Shirai, the king is named "Great King Chen," and his daughter's name is also said to be named Hachiman.{{Cite web |title=神社啓蒙 7巻目録1巻. The local people then took pity on those who had died in a different land, and built mounds to comfort their souls at the places where they had fallen. These mounds are located in the northern part of the Kokubu Plain in Kagoshima Prefecture. There are several other legends concerning the Usa Hachiman emissary that differ in content from the above. This happened again in 1874, and once more in 1895 when it was promoted to a Grand Shrine. After the war, the shrine became a part of the Association of Shinto Shrines. The following year, February 9, 2022, this was reported in the official gazette and they were officially designated as Important Cultural Properties.{{Cite web |last=霧島市 |title=国宝・重要文化財(建造物)の指定について |url=http://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kokuhoukettei.html |access-date=2022-09-29 |website=霧島市 |language=ja}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons category|Kagoshima-jingu|Kagoshima Shrine}} * {{OSM|n|4459864389}} {{Shinto shrine}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kagoshima Prefecture]] [[Category:Kanpei Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai Taisha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Kagoshima Prefecture]]
