Rice planting festival|Map = {{Location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kagoshima Shrine|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=12|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|frame-height=200|frame-latitude=31.751|frame-longitude=130.742}} }} [[File:Kagoshima-jingu, otorii.jpg|thumb|280px|right|{{center|Otorii}}]]'''Kagoshima Jingu'' (Kagoshima Jingu) is a shrine located in {{jalink|Kagoshima Prefecture|Q15701}}{{jalink|Kirishima City|Q858352}} Hayato Town. {{jalink|Shikinai Taisha|Q134917288}} ({{jalink|Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932|Kokuhei Taisha}}), {{jalink|Osumi Province|Q981002}}{{jalink|Ichinomiya|Q1656379}}. {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System#Government Shrine|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}, and currently it is {{jalink|Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shrine Head Office|Q908077}}. In the past, it was also called ``Osumi Sho Hachiman Shrine'' and ``Kokubu Hachiman Shrine.'' === Enshrined God === The current deities enshrined are as follows [http://kagoshima-jingu.jp/yuisyo.php About the history] (official website). . ; Main enshrined deity :* '''{{jalink|hoori|Q1051960|Amatsu Hidakahikohohodemi-no-mikoto}}''' :* '''{{jalink|Toyota Mahime|Q2329261|Toyota Hime no Mikoto}}''' (Toyota Hime no Mikoto) - Empress of Amatsu Hidakahiko Hidemi no Mikoto. ; Aidenjin :* {{jalink|Emperor Chuai|Q179971|Obichuhiko no Mikoto}} (Mikoto Nakatarashihiko, the 14th Emperor Chuai) :* {{jalink|Empress Jingu|Q232803|Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto}} (Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto, Empress Jingu) - Empress of Emperor Chuai. :* {{jalink|Emperor Ojin|Q317997|Shinada Wakeson}} (Mikoto Homuda, 15th Emperor Ojin, Hachiman Okami) :* {{jalink|Nakahime no Mikoto|Q11378496|Nakahime no Mikoto}} (Nakatsuhime no Mikoto, Nakahime no Mikoto) - Empress of Emperor Ojin. : The four pillars of Aidenjin are based on the relationship that {{jalink|Hachimanjin|Q261637}} is enshrined together. === History === According to the shrine's legend, it was founded in the distant {{jalink|the age of the gods|Q3577055}}, or ``during the reign of {{jalink|Emperor Jinmu|Q200188}}, it was built as a shrine at Takachiho-gu, which was the palace of {{jalink|Hoori|Q1051960|Amatsu Hidakahiko Hohoidemiko}}.'' It was moved to its current location in the first year of {{jalink|Wado|Q1373026}} ({{jalink|708|Q23511}}), and currently {{jalink|Setsusha|Q135009904}}'''Ishitai Shrine'' (Ishitai Shrine) is located on the former site. At a point 13km northwest of our company, there is {{jalink|Takayasanjo Mausoleum|Q11669273}}, which is said to be the {{jalink|Emperor's Mausoleum|Q17218816|Autumn}} of {{jalink|Hoori|Q1051960|Hoho Demikoto}}.The first appearance in reliable historical materials is in "{{jalink|Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932}}," which was compiled during the reign of Emperor Daigo|Q329753} as follows: Kagoshima Shrine" and is listed as a major shrine, and the so-called In {jalink|Southern Kyushu|Q8017707}}, it is the only {{jalink|Shikinai Taisha|Q134917288}} ({{jalink|Engishiki Jinmyocho|Q11064932|Kokuhei Taisha}}). Due to its high status, the Shinto priesthood produced influential {{jalink|national people|Q859955}} such as the {{jalink|Kuwahata clan}} and the {{jalink|Taxosho clan}}. In the {{jalink|Kenkyu|Q1193933|Kenkyu era}} (1190 - 1199), there was a company territory of over 2,500 {{jalink|town (unit)|Q1185752|machibu}}, and until the end of the Edo period, it had 1,000 {{jalink|stone height|Q909302|stone}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/tanbou/28/ |title=Kagoshima Shrine |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefectural Shrine Agency}}.{{jalink|Oei|Q1193564}} 7 ({{jalink|1527|Q6412}}) Because it was destroyed by military fire, {{jalink|astronomical (era name)|Q1192853|Tenbun}} In the 20th year ({{jalink|1551|Q6560}}), {{jalink|Emperor Konara|Q349467}} obtained {{jalink|reji|Q11607250}}, and {{jalink|Takahisa Shimazu|Q2367308}} became {{jalink|Nishide (Shingon Buddhism)|Q20042042|Nisshu Shonin}} was ordered to rebuild the shrine, and on December 13, 3rd year of {{jalink|Eiroku|Q1143341}} ({{jalink|1560|Q6613}}), the shrine was moved to the newly constructed shrine building.{{Cite web |title=National Diet Library Digital Collection |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/992141/1/18 |website=dl.ndl.go.jp |access-date=2024-05-28}}. From {{jalink|Sengoku period (Japan)|Q204023|Sengoku period}} to {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}}, it was revered by the {{jalink|Shimadzu clan|Q1061406}}, the local {{jalink|Daimyo|Q61982}}.In {{jalink|1871|Q7746|1871}}{{jalink|year|Q577}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}4), it was ranked as a Kokuhei Chusha shrine as ``Shikajima Shrine'' in {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}} by the Meiji government. In {{jalink|1874|Q7761}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}7), the {{jalink|Jingu|Q120680118}} was declared and {{jali nk|Modern shrine rank system|Q712534}}, it was ranked as {{jalink|Kanpei Chusha}} and was promoted to Kanpei Taisha in {{jalink|1895|Q7844}} (Meiji 28). After the war, it became {{jalink|Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shinja Honcho|Q908077}}. {{jalink|1935|Q18658}} (Showa 10) {{jalink|November 10|Q2988}}, {{jalink|Emperor Showa|Q34479}}, who is participating in the {{jalink|Special Army Exercise}}, visits the train. |publisher=Shinchosha |year=2016-09-30 |page=77 |isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}.{{jalink|2021|Q49628}} ({{jalink|Reiwa|Q62609017}}3) November 19th, National {{jalink|Cultural Council|Q1 1499811}} recommends that the main shrine, worship hall, imperial envoy hall, and main shrine of Sessha Shisho Shrine be designated as {{jalink|Important Cultural Properties|Q1188622}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kokuho-jubun.html |title=About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) |publisher=Kirishima City |date=2021-10-29 |accessdate=2022-02-11}}. The following year, it was announced in {{jalink|Official Gazette|Q11452096}} on February 9, 2022, and it was officially designated as an important cultural property.{{cite news|title=Kirishima Shrine officially designated as a national treasure. Kagoshima Shrine also designated as an important cultural property |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209055427/https://www3.nhk.or.jp/lnews/kagoshima/20220209/5050017814.html |publisher= {{jalink|Japan Broadcasting Corporation|Q212128}} (NHK NEWS WEB) |date=2022-02-09 |accessdate=2022-02-11}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|date=2022-02-09 |url=http://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kokuhoukettei.html |title=About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) |publisher=Kirishima City |accessdate=2022-02-11}}. === Enshrinement of Hachiman God === It is also said that in the {{jalink|Heian period|Q193292}}, when {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} solicited the Yawata Bekku shrines of the five places in Kyushu, the {{jalink|Hachiman deity|Q261637}} was enshrined in our company. Since then, it has also been called Sho Hachiman Shrine, Osumi Sho Hachiman Shrine, {{jalink|Kokufu Hachiman Shrine|Q11420856|Kokubu Hachiman Shrine}}. In the "{{jalink|Konjaku Monogatari Shu|Q1507085}}" compiled in the late Heian period, {{jalink|Hachiman God|Q261637}} is {{jalink|Osumi Province|Q981002} }, then moved to {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa}}, and finally left its mark at {{jalink|Iwashimizu Hachimangu|Q710098|Iwashimizu}}.{{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q 329792}}5 ({{jalink|544|Q31012}}), it is said that {{jalink|Hachimanjin|Q261637}} was worshiped at this former shrine. ``When Ohirume, the daughter of the great king of Shintan Province ({{jalink|China|Q29520}} as seen from {{jalink|India|Q668}}), was seven years old, the morning sun pierced her chest, she became pregnant and gave birth to a prince.The king's retainers became suspicious of this, put her on an empty ship, and took the place where the ship was as their territory. The ship eventually arrived at a rocky shore in Chinzei, Japan, and the prince was named Hachiman.It is said that this was during the reign of Emperor Keitai. Furthermore, in ``{{jalink|Shrine Enlightenment}}'' written by {{jalink|Shirai Soin}}, the character is listed as ``Chen the Great,'' and his daughter's name is said to be Hachiman.Kagoshima Shrine is also said to be the original headquarters of Hachiman Shrine, as indicated by the positive character of Osumi Sho Hachiman. Legend has it that there was once a dispute between Kokubun Hachiman and {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} over which one was the legitimate Hachiman, and {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} secretly sent 15 (all 14) messengers to burn down Kokubun Hachiman. At that time, the character ``Sho Hachiman'' appeared in the black smoke rising from the burning shrine, and the messengers, shocked and frightened by this, fled to the land of {{jalink|Mizobe Town|Q11564513|Mizobe}}, but as if they had been punished by God, they fell down one after another, reaching 13 people in number. Afterwards, the local people took pity on those who died in a foreign land, and built mounds at the places where each of them had fallen to comfort the spirits.Since there were 13 mounds, it is said that they named the place {{jalink|Jusanzukahara|Q11404752}}. This {{jalink|Jusanzukahara|Q11404752}} is located in the north of {{jalink|Kokubu Plain|Q11420534}} of {{jalink|Kagoshima Prefecture|Q15701}}, and in the northeast of it there is {{jalink|Kagoshima Airport|Q1156310}} and Jusanzukahara Historical Park based on this legend. There are several other legends about the messenger of {{jalink|Usa Shrine|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} that differ from the above. === Precincts === [[File:Sangoku meisho zue Kagoshima Shrine.jpg|Thumbnail|450x450 pixels|Kagoshima Shrine in the Edo period ("{{jalink|Sangoku Scenic View|Q11354726}}"). ]] * Otorii - Torii that straddles a public road * Dedicated wooden horse - A sacred horse (wooden horse) dedicated in 1945.According to the information board installed on site. . * Shinbasha * Chozuya* Main shrine, worship hall, imperial envoy hall - Important cultural properties. The shrine building, which was built in 1601, suffered severe damage from termites, so construction was started in 1755 with a donation from Shigetoshi Shimazu, and the construction was completed the following year under Shigego Shimazu{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shittebunkazai/bunka-hayato.html#5 |title=Kagoshima Shrine Main Hall and Worship Hall Imperial Mission Hall Sessha Shisho Shrine Main Hall |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kirishima City Hall Education Department Social Education Division Cultural Properties Group}}. The imperial envoy hall corresponds to the entrance to the main shrine building, and is lined up with the worship hall and main shrine on the north side. Each building has rich decorations, with a dragon carried in the hall of imperial envoys and a ceiling painting in the hall of worship.The main hall is extremely large, and the whole is decorated with carvings and murals by Tangen Kimura, a painter of the Satsuma domain.It is finished in rich colors and lacquer, and a dragon carving is wrapped around the pillar of the prayer hall.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.kagoshima.jp/ba08/documents/62592_20220210110955-1.pdf |title=Kagoshima Jingu Main Hall and Worship Hall, Imperial Envoy Hall, Sessha Shisho Shrine Main Hall |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture |format=PDF}}. Furthermore, this {{jalink|Dragon Pillar|Q60985310}} has four claws, making it unique compared to other shrines in southern Kyushu that have dragon pillars that have three claws.* Rebuilt stone lantern at the main shrine - Prefecturally designated tangible cultural property. A lantern donated to the main shrine (currently Kagoshima Jingu) in 1756. It is a stone lantern with two legs and is called a ``kotobashira lantern''. |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kirishima City Hall Education Department Social Education Division Cultural Properties Group}}. On the front side of the leg, there is an inscription about the construction of the shrine . * Kanda * Sacred Tree - {{jalink|Kenkyu|Q1193933|Kenkyu Year}} The tree is said to be about 800 years old. * Kameishi * Hayato History and Folklore Museum - There is a history exhibition room, a folklore exhibition room, and a Japanese-style room. Documents related to Kagoshima Jingu Shrine, archaeological materials such as earthenware and stone axes excavated in Hayato Town, and materials and folk tools related to local performing arts such as the bell-kake horse dance are displayed, and the Japanese-style room recreates the atmosphere of the Showa era.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/shisetsu/kyoiku/028.html |title=Hayato History and Folklore Museum |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kirishima City Hall}}. * Shrine office * Yoseikan === Setsusha === * Shisho Shrine - Important cultural property. Enshrined deities: {{jalink|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|Daisaku no Mikoto}}, {{jalink|Ishihime no Mikoto|Q11585498|Ishihime no Mikoto}}, Arata Rōme, Netori no Mikoto. Annual festival: November 15th. * Takeuchi Shrine - Enshrined deity: Takeuchi Sukune. * Hayabusa Shrine - Enshrined deity: Nihon Takemyo. * Sannosha - Three shrines are built in front of the torii gate at the entrance to the shrine grounds. * Mikado Shrine - Two shrines are built at the foot of the stone steps to the shrine grounds. * Amenosha - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Watatsumi|Q1474187|Toyotamahiko no Mikoto}}. Regular festival: October 11th. * Shokonsha * Inari Shrine * Yamakami Shrine * Otarachi Goddess Shrine * Takachiho Shrine Ruins/Ishitama Shrine - The former shrine of Kagoshima Jingu. This is where the main hall of Takachiho Palace was located. * Hoshoku Shrine === Gallery === File:Kagoshima-jingu, shaden.jpg|alt=|Shrine

{{small|Kagoshima Jingu Motomiya traditional site. }} File:Kagoshima-jingu, Kuwahatashi-yakata-ato.jpg|Shake Kuwahatashi House Ruins (among national historic sites) File:Kagoshima-jingu, Mirokuin-ato.jpg|Mirokuin ruins (among national historic sites) === Festival === [[File:Hatsu uma sai 02.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Hatsuuma sai (photographed in 2012)]] The annual festivals held at Kagoshima Shrine are as follows. . * Seven Kinds Festival (January 7th) * {{jalink|Hatsuuma Festival (Kagoshima Shrine)|Q11396442|Hatsuuma Festival}} (January 18th of the lunar calendar: In recent years, it has been a recent Sunday) * Fuji Festival (March 10th of the lunar calendar) * Rice planting festival (May 5th of the lunar calendar) * Annual festival (August 15th of the lunar calendar) * Tanabata Festival * Mihama Kudari Festival (3rd Sunday in October) === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Kagoshima Shrine 3 buildings (1 attached ridge tag) (buildings) - Construction began in 1755 with a donation from {{jalink|Shimadzu Shigetoshi|Q11476823}}. It was completed the following year during the reign of {{jalink|Shigego Shimazu|Q8013051}}. Designated on February 9, 2022 (Reiwa 4)Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 10, February 9, 2022. [https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shitebunkazai/bunka-hayato.html#5 Cultural property [Hayato]] (Kirishima City homepage, updated on February 8, 2022). ** Main shrine and worship hall ** Imperial Envoy Hall ** Sessha Shisho Shrine Main Hall * Dark blue armor with helmet and large sleeves (craft) *: Dedicated by Yukihisa Kabayama, chief retainer of the Shimazu clan. Designated on March 31, 1953 {{Nationally designated cultural property database|201|5547|Navy blue armor with helmet and large sleeves/>}}. * Various Idomaru helmets with large sleeves (crafts) *: Dedicated by Takahisa Shimazu in 1558. {{jalink|Kagoshima Prefectural Historical Materials Center Reimeikan}} Stored. Designated on March 31, 1953 {{Nationally Designated Cultural Properties Database|201|5548|Various Idomaru (helmet with large sleeves)}}. * Various Idomaru helmets with large sleeves (crafts)*: Dedicated by Takahisa Shimazu in 1558. Stored at Tokyo National Museum. Designated on March 31, 1953{{Nationally designated cultural property database|201|5549|Various Idomaru (helmet with large sleeves/)}}. * Sword Mumei (Den Norishige) (craft) *: Its whereabouts were unknown after it was requisitioned by the Occupation Forces after the war, but a sword with matching characteristics was found in Australia in 2022.{{cite news|title=Former National Treasure Sword Found in Australia? GHQ requisitioned after the war, whereabouts unknown |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220223195910/https://www3.nhk.or.jp/news/html/20220224/k10013498361000.html |publisher=Japan Broadcasting Corporation (NHK NEWS WEB) |date=2022-02-24 |accessdate=2022-03-03}}. Designated on April 8, 1918 (Taisho 7) {{Nationally Designated Cultural Properties Database|201|10468|Sword }}. * Sword, famous Sōshū Sumiakihiro Meitokusan (craft)*: Written in 1392. Dedicated by the 27th Shimazu Saioki. After the war, it was confiscated by the Occupation Forces and its whereabouts were unknown, but it was discovered at an auction and bought back by the shrine in 2003. Currently stored at Reimeikan, Kagoshima Prefectural Historical Materials Center. Designated on April 25, 1927. === National Historic Site === * Osumi Sho Hachiman Shrine Precincts and Shrine Remains - Designated on October 17, 2013 {{Nationally Designated Cultural Properties Database|401|00003825|Osumi Sho Hachiman Shrine Precincts and Shrine Remains}}. === Intangible folk cultural properties selected by the country{{jalink|Intangible folk cultural properties for which measures such as recording should be taken|Q11642584}} === * {{jalink|Hatsuuma Festival (Kagoshima Shrine)|Q11396442|Customs of horse dance in Satsuma}} - Selected on February 12, 2002 (Heisei 14){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/312/753 |title=Customs of horse dance in Satsuma / Intangible folk cultural properties for which measures such as recording should be taken |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Nationally designated cultural properties database / Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. === Cultural property designated by Kagoshima Prefecture === *Tangible cultural property ** Stone lantern (structure) in the main shrine reconstruction **: Designated on April 22, 2014 . ** Ceramics (crafts) owned by Kagoshima Jingu Shrine **: On March 25, 2008, it was designated as a Kirishima City-designated tangible cultural property (craft) as "Kagoshima Shrine Treasure Ceramics," and on April 23, 2010, it was designated as a Kagoshima Prefecture-designated tangible cultural property . ** Kagoshima Shrine Documents (Ancient Documents) **: Letter of appointment of Sho Hachiman Shrine priestess, letter of Seal of Sho Hachiman Shrine, letter of appointment of Seitoki Sakai for repair of the main shrine, letter of appointment of Tameharu Sakai of Hachiman Shrine repair office. Designated on March 16, 1987 [https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shittebunkazai/ichiran.html List of designated (registered) cultural assets] (Kirishima City homepage, updated on February 17, 2021). *Tangible folk cultural properties ** The god of rice fields in the shrine **: Designated on March 29, 1968 (Showa 43). === Kirishima City designated cultural property === *Tangible cultural property ** Hoshoku Shrine (building) at Tsuji-no-Kado - Originally Benzaiten-do Hall at Shirasagi Pond next to Miroku-in Temple. It was moved to its current location during the Meiji period during the Haibutsu-kishaku movement. Designated on July 6, 2005 . ** Kagoshima Jingu Four Heavenly Kings Stone Statues (Historical Materials) - Found at the Hayato History and Folklore Museum. Stored at Hayatozuka Historical Museum. Designated on June 7, 1994 . ** Jingu Old Seal (Historical Material) - Designated on July 3, 1995 . * Historic sites ** Miyasaka Shell Midden - A shell midden discovered on the back approach. Designated on December 8, 1999 . * Intangible folk cultural assets ** {{jalink|Hatsuuma Festival (Kagoshima Shrine)|Q11396442|Horse of the Eighteenth Day}} - Designated on March 31, 1987 (Showa 62) . Rice planting festival|Map = {{Location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kagoshima Shrine|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=12|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|frame-height=200|frame-latitude=31.751|frame-longitude=130.742}} }} [[File:Kagoshima-jingu, otorii.jpg|thumb|280px|right|{{center|Otorii}}]]'''Kagoshima Jingu'' (Kagoshima Jingu) is a shrine located in {{jalink|Kagoshima Prefecture|Q15701}}{{jalink|Kirishima City|Q858352}} Hayato Town. {{jalink|Shikinai Taisha|Q134917288}} ({{jalink|Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932|Kokuhei Taisha}}), {{jalink|Osumi Province|Q981002}}{{jalink|Ichinomiya|Q1656379}}. {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System#Government Shrine|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}, and currently it is {{jalink|Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shrine Head Office|Q908077}}. In the past, it was also called ``Osumi Sho Hachiman Shrine'' and ``Kokubu Hachiman Shrine.'' === Enshrined God === The current deities enshrined are as follows [http://kagoshima-jingu.jp/yuisyo.php About the history] (official website). . ; Main enshrined deity :* '''{{jalink|hoori|Q1051960|Amatsu Hidakahikohohodemi-no-mikoto}}''' :* '''{{jalink|Toyota Mahime|Q2329261|Toyota Hime no Mikoto}}''' (Toyota Hime no Mikoto) - Empress of Amatsu Hidakahiko Hidemi no Mikoto. ; Aidenjin :* {{jalink|Emperor Chuai|Q179971|Obichuhiko no Mikoto}} (Mikoto Nakatarashihiko, the 14th Emperor Chuai) :* {{jalink|Empress Jingu|Q232803|Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto}} (Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto, Empress Jingu) - Empress of Emperor Chuai. :* {{jalink|Emperor Ojin|Q317997|Shinada Wakeson}} (Mikoto Homuda, 15th Emperor Ojin, Hachiman Okami) :* {{jalink|Nakahime no Mikoto|Q11378496|Nakahime no Mikoto}} (Nakatsuhime no Mikoto, Nakahime no Mikoto) - Empress of Emperor Ojin. : The four pillars of Aidenjin are based on the relationship that {{jalink|Hachimanjin|Q261637}} is enshrined together. === History === According to the shrine's legend, it was founded in the distant {{jalink|the age of the gods|Q3577055}}, or ``during the reign of {{jalink|Emperor Jinmu|Q200188}}, it was built as a shrine at Takachiho-gu, which was the palace of {{jalink|Hoori|Q1051960|Amatsu Hidakahiko Hohoidemiko}}.'' It was moved to its current location in the first year of {{jalink|Wado|Q1373026}} ({{jalink|708|Q23511}}), and currently {{jalink|Setsusha|Q135009904}}'''Ishitai Shrine'' (Ishitai Shrine) is located on the former site. At a point 13km northwest of our company, there is {{jalink|Takayasanjo Mausoleum|Q11669273}}, which is said to be the {{jalink|Emperor's Mausoleum|Q17218816|Autumn}} of {{jalink|Hoori|Q1051960|Hoho Demikoto}}.The first appearance in reliable historical materials is in "{{jalink|Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932}}," which was compiled during the reign of Emperor Daigo|Q329753} as follows: Kagoshima Shrine" and is listed as a major shrine, and the so-called In {jalink|Southern Kyushu|Q8017707}}, it is the only {{jalink|Shikinai Taisha|Q134917288}} ({{jalink|Engishiki Jinmyocho|Q11064932|Kokuhei Taisha}}). Due to its high status, the Shinto priesthood produced influential {{jalink|national people|Q859955}} such as the {{jalink|Kuwahata clan}} and the {{jalink|Taxosho clan}}. In the {{jalink|Kenkyu|Q1193933|Kenkyu era}} (1190 - 1199), there was a company territory of over 2,500 {{jalink|town (unit)|Q1185752|machibu}}, and until the end of the Edo period, it had 1,000 {{jalink|stone height|Q909302|stone}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/tanbou/28/ |title=Kagoshima Shrine |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefectural Shrine Agency}}.{{jalink|Oei|Q1193564}} 7 ({{jalink|1527|Q6412}}) Because it was destroyed by military fire, {{jalink|astronomical (era name)|Q1192853|Tenbun}} In the 20th year ({{jalink|1551|Q6560}}), {{jalink|Emperor Konara|Q349467}} obtained {{jalink|reji|Q11607250}}, and {{jalink|Takahisa Shimazu|Q2367308}} became {{jalink|Nishide (Shingon Buddhism)|Q20042042|Nisshu Shonin}} was ordered to rebuild the shrine, and on December 13, 3rd year of {{jalink|Eiroku|Q1143341}} ({{jalink|1560|Q6613}}), the shrine was moved to the newly constructed shrine building.{{Cite web |title=National Diet Library Digital Collection |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/992141/1/18 |website=dl.ndl.go.jp |access-date=2024-05-28}}. From {{jalink|Sengoku period (Japan)|Q204023|Sengoku period}} to {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}}, it was revered by the {{jalink|Shimadzu clan|Q1061406}}, the local {{jalink|Daimyo|Q61982}}.In {{jalink|1871|Q7746|1871}}{{jalink|year|Q577}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}4), it was ranked as a Kokuhei Chusha shrine as ``Shikajima Shrine'' in {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}} by the Meiji government. In {{jalink|1874|Q7761}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}7), the {{jalink|Jingu|Q120680118}} was declared and {{jali nk|Modern shrine rank system|Q712534}}, it was ranked as {{jalink|Kanpei Chusha}} and was promoted to Kanpei Taisha in {{jalink|1895|Q7844}} (Meiji 28). After the war, it became {{jalink|Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shinja Honcho|Q908077}}. {{jalink|1935|Q18658}} (Showa 10) {{jalink|November 10|Q2988}}, {{jalink|Emperor Showa|Q34479}}, who is participating in the {{jalink|Special Army Exercise}}, visits the train. |publisher=Shinchosha |year=2016-09-30 |page=77 |isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}.{{jalink|2021|Q49628}} ({{jalink|Reiwa|Q62609017}}3) November 19th, National {{jalink|Cultural Council|Q1 1499811}} recommends that the main shrine, worship hall, imperial envoy hall, and main shrine of Sessha Shisho Shrine be designated as {{jalink|Important Cultural Properties|Q1188622}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kokuho-jubun.html |title=About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) |publisher=Kirishima City |date=2021-10-29 |accessdate=2022-02-11}}. The following year, it was announced in {{jalink|Official Gazette|Q11452096}} on February 9, 2022, and it was officially designated as an important cultural property.{{cite news|title=Kirishima Shrine officially designated as a national treasure. Kagoshima Shrine also designated as an important cultural property |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209055427/https://www3.nhk.or.jp/lnews/kagoshima/20220209/5050017814.html |publisher= {{jalink|Japan Broadcasting Corporation|Q212128}} (NHK NEWS WEB) |date=2022-02-09 |accessdate=2022-02-11}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|date=2022-02-09 |url=http://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kokuhoukettei.html |title=About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) |publisher=Kirishima City |accessdate=2022-02-11}}. === Enshrinement of Hachiman God === It is also said that in the {{jalink|Heian period|Q193292}}, when {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} solicited the Yawata Bekku shrines of the five places in Kyushu, the {{jalink|Hachiman deity|Q261637}} was enshrined in our company. Since then, it has also been called Sho Hachiman Shrine, Osumi Sho Hachiman Shrine, {{jalink|Kokufu Hachiman Shrine|Q11420856|Kokubu Hachiman Shrine}}. In the "{{jalink|Konjaku Monogatari Shu|Q1507085}}" compiled in the late Heian period, {{jalink|Hachiman God|Q261637}} is {{jalink|Osumi Province|Q981002} }, then moved to {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa}}, and finally left its mark at {{jalink|Iwashimizu Hachimangu|Q710098|Iwashimizu}}.{{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q 329792}}5 ({{jalink|544|Q31012}}), it is said that {{jalink|Hachimanjin|Q261637}} was worshiped at this former shrine. ``When Ohirume, the daughter of the great king of Shintan Province ({{jalink|China|Q29520}} as seen from {{jalink|India|Q668}}), was seven years old, the morning sun pierced her chest, she became pregnant and gave birth to a prince.The king's retainers became suspicious of this, put her on an empty ship, and took the place where the ship was as their territory. The ship eventually arrived at a rocky shore in Chinzei, Japan, and the prince was named Hachiman.It is said that this was during the reign of Emperor Keitai. Furthermore, in ``{{jalink|Shrine Enlightenment}}'' written by {{jalink|Shirai Soin}}, the character is listed as ``Chen the Great,'' and his daughter's name is said to be Hachiman.Kagoshima Shrine is also said to be the original headquarters of Hachiman Shrine, as indicated by the positive character of Osumi Sho Hachiman. Legend has it that there was once a dispute between Kokubun Hachiman and {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} over which one was the legitimate Hachiman, and {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} secretly sent 15 (all 14) messengers to burn down Kokubun Hachiman. At that time, the character ``Sho Hachiman'' appeared in the black smoke rising from the burning shrine, and the messengers, shocked and frightened by this, fled to the land of {{jalink|Mizobe Town|Q11564513|Mizobe}}, but as if they had been punished by God, they fell down one after another, reaching 13 people in number. Afterwards, the local people took pity on those who died in a foreign land, and built mounds at the places where each of them had fallen to comfort the spirits.Since there were 13 mounds, it is said that they named the place {{jalink|Jusanzukahara|Q11404752}}. This {{jalink|Jusanzukahara|Q11404752}} is located in the north of {{jalink|Kokubu Plain|Q11420534}} of {{jalink|Kagoshima Prefecture|Q15701}}, and in the northeast of it there is {{jalink|Kagoshima Airport|Q1156310}} and Jusanzukahara Historical Park based on this legend. There are several other legends about the messenger of {{jalink|Usa Shrine|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} that differ from the above. === Precincts === [[File:Sangoku meisho zue Kagoshima Shrine.jpg|Thumbnail|450x450 pixels|Kagoshima Shrine in the Edo period ("{{jalink|Sangoku Scenic View|Q11354726}}"). ]] * Otorii - Torii that straddles a public road * Dedicated wooden horse - A sacred horse (wooden horse) dedicated in 1945.According to the information board installed on site. . * Shinbasha * Chozuya* Main shrine, worship hall, imperial envoy hall - Important cultural properties. The shrine building, which was built in 1601, suffered severe damage from termites, so construction was started in 1755 with a donation from Shigetoshi Shimazu, and the construction was completed the following year under Shigego Shimazu{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shittebunkazai/bunka-hayato.html#5 |title=Kagoshima Shrine Main Hall and Worship Hall Imperial Mission Hall Sessha Shisho Shrine Main Hall |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kirishima City Hall Education Department Social Education Division Cultural Properties Group}}. The imperial envoy hall corresponds to the entrance to the main shrine building, and is lined up with the worship hall and main shrine on the north side. Each building has rich decorations, with a dragon carried in the hall of imperial envoys and a ceiling painting in the hall of worship.The main hall is extremely large, and the whole is decorated with carvings and murals by Tangen Kimura, a painter of the Satsuma domain.It is finished in rich colors and lacquer, and a dragon carving is wrapped around the pillar of the prayer hall.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.kagoshima.jp/ba08/documents/62592_20220210110955-1.pdf |title=Kagoshima Jingu Main Hall and Worship Hall, Imperial Envoy Hall, Sessha Shisho Shrine Main Hall |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture |format=PDF}}. Furthermore, this {{jalink|Dragon Pillar|Q60985310}} has four claws, making it unique compared to other shrines in southern Kyushu that have dragon pillars that have three claws.* Rebuilt stone lantern at the main shrine - Prefecturally designated tangible cultural property. A lantern donated to the main shrine (currently Kagoshima Jingu) in 1756. It is a stone lantern with two legs and is called a ``kotobashira lantern''. |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kirishima City Hall Education Department Social Education Division Cultural Properties Group}}. On the front side of the leg, there is an inscription about the construction of the shrine . * Kanda * Sacred Tree - {{jalink|Kenkyu|Q1193933|Kenkyu Year}} The tree is said to be about 800 years old. * Kameishi * Hayato History and Folklore Museum - There is a history exhibition room, a folklore exhibition room, and a Japanese-style room. Documents related to Kagoshima Jingu Shrine, archaeological materials such as earthenware and stone axes excavated in Hayato Town, and materials and folk tools related to local performing arts such as the bell-kake horse dance are displayed, and the Japanese-style room recreates the atmosphere of the Showa era.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/shisetsu/kyoiku/028.html |title=Hayato History and Folklore Museum |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kirishima City Hall}}. * Shrine office * Yoseikan === Setsusha === * Shisho Shrine - Important cultural property. Enshrined deities: {{jalink|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|Daisaku no Mikoto}}, {{jalink|Ishihime no Mikoto|Q11585498|Ishihime no Mikoto}}, Arata Rōme, Netori no Mikoto. Annual festival: November 15th. * Takeuchi Shrine - Enshrined deity: Takeuchi Sukune. * Hayabusa Shrine - Enshrined deity: Nihon Takemyo. * Sannosha - Three shrines are built in front of the torii gate at the entrance to the shrine grounds. * Mikado Shrine - Two shrines are built at the foot of the stone steps to the shrine grounds. * Amenosha - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Watatsumi|Q1474187|Toyotamahiko no Mikoto}}. Regular festival: October 11th. * Shokonsha * Inari Shrine * Yamakami Shrine * Otarachi Goddess Shrine * Takachiho Shrine Ruins/Ishitama Shrine - The former shrine of Kagoshima Jingu. This is where the main hall of Takachiho Palace was located. * Hoshoku Shrine === Gallery === File:Kagoshima-jingu, shaden.jpg|alt=|Shrine

{{small|Kagoshima Jingu Motomiya traditional site. }} File:Kagoshima-jingu, Kuwahatashi-yakata-ato.jpg|Shake Kuwahatashi House Ruins (among national historic sites) File:Kagoshima-jingu, Mirokuin-ato.jpg|Mirokuin ruins (among national historic sites) === Festival === [[File:Hatsu uma sai 02.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Hatsuuma sai (photographed in 2012)]] The annual festivals held at Kagoshima Shrine are as follows. . * Seven Kinds Festival (January 7th) * {{jalink|Hatsuuma Festival (Kagoshima Shrine)|Q11396442|Hatsuuma Festival}} (January 18th of the lunar calendar: In recent years, it has been a recent Sunday) * Fuji Festival (March 10th of the lunar calendar) * Rice planting festival (May 5th of the lunar calendar) * Annual festival (August 15th of the lunar calendar) * Tanabata Festival * Mihama Kudari Festival (3rd Sunday in October) === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Kagoshima Shrine 3 buildings (1 attached ridge tag) (buildings) - Construction began in 1755 with a donation from {{jalink|Shimadzu Shigetoshi|Q11476823}}. It was completed the following year during the reign of {{jalink|Shigego Shimazu|Q8013051}}. Designated on February 9, 2022 (Reiwa 4)Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 10, February 9, 2022. [https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shitebunkazai/bunka-hayato.html#5 Cultural property [Hayato]] (Kirishima City homepage, updated on February 8, 2022). ** Main shrine and worship hall ** Imperial Envoy Hall ** Sessha Shisho Shrine Main Hall * Dark blue armor with helmet and large sleeves (craft) *: Dedicated by Yukihisa Kabayama, chief retainer of the Shimazu clan. Designated on March 31, 1953 {{Nationally designated cultural property database|201|5547|Navy blue armor with helmet and large sleeves/>}}. * Various Idomaru helmets with large sleeves (crafts) *: Dedicated by Takahisa Shimazu in 1558. {{jalink|Kagoshima Prefectural Historical Materials Center Reimeikan}} Stored. Designated on March 31, 1953 {{Nationally Designated Cultural Properties Database|201|5548|Various Idomaru (helmet with large sleeves)}}. * Various Idomaru helmets with large sleeves (crafts)*: Dedicated by Takahisa Shimazu in 1558. Stored at Tokyo National Museum. Designated on March 31, 1953{{Nationally designated cultural property database|201|5549|Various Idomaru (helmet with large sleeves/)}}. * Sword Mumei (Den Norishige) (craft) *: Its whereabouts were unknown after it was requisitioned by the Occupation Forces after the war, but a sword with matching characteristics was found in Australia in 2022.{{cite news|title=Former National Treasure Sword Found in Australia? GHQ requisitioned after the war, whereabouts unknown |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220223195910/https://www3.nhk.or.jp/news/html/20220224/k10013498361000.html |publisher=Japan Broadcasting Corporation (NHK NEWS WEB) |date=2022-02-24 |accessdate=2022-03-03}}. Designated on April 8, 1918 (Taisho 7) {{Nationally Designated Cultural Properties Database|201|10468|Sword }}. * Sword, famous Sōshū Sumiakihiro Meitokusan (craft)*: Written in 1392. Dedicated by the 27th Shimazu Saioki. After the war, it was confiscated by the Occupation Forces and its whereabouts were unknown, but it was discovered at an auction and bought back by the shrine in 2003. Currently stored at Reimeikan, Kagoshima Prefectural Historical Materials Center. Designated on April 25, 1927. === National Historic Site === * Osumi Sho Hachiman Shrine Precincts and Shrine Remains - Designated on October 17, 2013 {{Nationally Designated Cultural Properties Database|401|00003825|Osumi Sho Hachiman Shrine Precincts and Shrine Remains}}. === Intangible folk cultural properties selected by the country{{jalink|Intangible folk cultural properties for which measures such as recording should be taken|Q11642584}} === * {{jalink|Hatsuuma Festival (Kagoshima Shrine)|Q11396442|Customs of horse dance in Satsuma}} - Selected on February 12, 2002 (Heisei 14){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/312/753 |title=Customs of horse dance in Satsuma / Intangible folk cultural properties for which measures such as recording should be taken |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Nationally designated cultural properties database / Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. === Cultural property designated by Kagoshima Prefecture === *Tangible cultural property ** Stone lantern (structure) in the main shrine reconstruction **: Designated on April 22, 2014 . ** Ceramics (crafts) owned by Kagoshima Jingu Shrine **: On March 25, 2008, it was designated as a Kirishima City-designated tangible cultural property (craft) as "Kagoshima Shrine Treasure Ceramics," and on April 23, 2010, it was designated as a Kagoshima Prefecture-designated tangible cultural property . ** Kagoshima Shrine Documents (Ancient Documents) **: Letter of appointment of Sho Hachiman Shrine priestess, letter of Seal of Sho Hachiman Shrine, letter of appointment of Seitoki Sakai for repair of the main shrine, letter of appointment of Tameharu Sakai of Hachiman Shrine repair office. Designated on March 16, 1987 [https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shittebunkazai/ichiran.html List of designated (registered) cultural assets] (Kirishima City homepage, updated on February 17, 2021). *Tangible folk cultural properties ** The god of rice fields in the shrine **: Designated on March 29, 1968 (Showa 43). === Kirishima City designated cultural property === *Tangible cultural property ** Hoshoku Shrine (building) at Tsuji-no-Kado - Originally Benzaiten-do Hall at Shirasagi Pond next to Miroku-in Temple. It was moved to its current location during the Meiji period during the Haibutsu-kishaku movement. Designated on July 6, 2005 . ** Kagoshima Jingu Four Heavenly Kings Stone Statues (Historical Materials) - Found at the Hayato History and Folklore Museum. Stored at Hayatozuka Historical Museum. Designated on June 7, 1994 . ** Jingu Old Seal (Historical Material) - Designated on July 3, 1995 . * Historic sites ** Miyasaka Shell Midden - A shell midden discovered on the back approach. Designated on December 8, 1999 . * Intangible folk cultural assets ** {{jalink|Hatsuuma Festival (Kagoshima Shrine)|Q11396442|Horse of the Eighteenth Day}} - Designated on March 31, 1987 (Showa 62) . Rice planting festival|Map = {{Location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kagoshima Shrine|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=12|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|frame-height=200|frame-latitude=31.751|frame-longitude=130.742}} }} [[File:Kagoshima-jingu, otorii.jpg|thumb|280px|right|{{center|Otorii}}]]'''Kagoshima Jingu'' (Kagoshima Jingu) is a shrine located in {{jalink|Kagoshima Prefecture|Q15701}}{{jalink|Kirishima City|Q858352}} Hayato Town. {{jalink|Shikinai Taisha|Q134917288}} ({{jalink|Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932|Kokuhei Taisha}}), {{jalink|Osumi Province|Q981002}}{{jalink|Ichinomiya|Q1656379}}. {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System#Government Shrine|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}, and currently it is {{jalink|Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shrine Head Office|Q908077}}. In the past, it was also called ``Osumi Sho Hachiman Shrine'' and ``Kokubu Hachiman Shrine.'' === Enshrined God === The current deities enshrined are as follows [http://kagoshima-jingu.jp/yuisyo.php About the history] (official website). . ; Main enshrined deity :* '''{{jalink|hoori|Q1051960|Amatsu Hidakahikohohodemi-no-mikoto}}''' :* '''{{jalink|Toyota Mahime|Q2329261|Toyota Hime no Mikoto}}''' (Toyota Hime no Mikoto) - Empress of Amatsu Hidakahiko Hidemi no Mikoto. ; Aidenjin :* {{jalink|Emperor Chuai|Q179971|Obichuhiko no Mikoto}} (Mikoto Nakatarashihiko, the 14th Emperor Chuai) :* {{jalink|Empress Jingu|Q232803|Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto}} (Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto, Empress Jingu) - Empress of Emperor Chuai. :* {{jalink|Emperor Ojin|Q317997|Shinada Wakeson}} (Mikoto Homuda, 15th Emperor Ojin, Hachiman Okami) :* {{jalink|Nakahime no Mikoto|Q11378496|Nakahime no Mikoto}} (Nakatsuhime no Mikoto, Nakahime no Mikoto) - Empress of Emperor Ojin. : The four pillars of Aidenjin are based on the relationship that {{jalink|Hachimanjin|Q261637}} is enshrined together. === History === According to the shrine's legend, it was founded in the distant {{jalink|the age of the gods|Q3577055}}, or ``during the reign of {{jalink|Emperor Jinmu|Q200188}}, it was built as a shrine at Takachiho-gu, which was the palace of {{jalink|Hoori|Q1051960|Amatsu Hidakahiko Hohoidemiko}}.'' It was moved to its current location in the first year of {{jalink|Wado|Q1373026}} ({{jalink|708|Q23511}}), and currently {{jalink|Setsusha|Q135009904}}'''Ishitai Shrine'' (Ishitai Shrine) is located on the former site. At a point 13km northwest of our company, there is {{jalink|Takayasanjo Mausoleum|Q11669273}}, which is said to be the {{jalink|Emperor's Mausoleum|Q17218816|Autumn}} of {{jalink|Hoori|Q1051960|Hoho Demikoto}}.The first appearance in reliable historical materials is in "{{jalink|Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932}}," which was compiled during the reign of Emperor Daigo|Q329753} as follows: Kagoshima Shrine" and is listed as a major shrine, and the so-called In {jalink|Southern Kyushu|Q8017707}}, it is the only {{jalink|Shikinai Taisha|Q134917288}} ({{jalink|Engishiki Jinmyocho|Q11064932|Kokuhei Taisha}}). Due to its high status, the Shinto priesthood produced influential {{jalink|national people|Q859955}} such as the {{jalink|Kuwahata clan}} and the {{jalink|Taxosho clan}}. In the {{jalink|Kenkyu|Q1193933|Kenkyu era}} (1190 - 1199), there was a company territory of over 2,500 {{jalink|town (unit)|Q1185752|machibu}}, and until the end of the Edo period, it had 1,000 {{jalink|stone height|Q909302|stone}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/tanbou/28/ |title=Kagoshima Shrine |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefectural Shrine Agency}}.{{jalink|Oei|Q1193564}} 7 ({{jalink|1527|Q6412}}) Because it was destroyed by military fire, {{jalink|astronomical (era name)|Q1192853|Tenbun}} In the 20th year ({{jalink|1551|Q6560}}), {{jalink|Emperor Konara|Q349467}} obtained {{jalink|reji|Q11607250}}, and {{jalink|Takahisa Shimazu|Q2367308}} became {{jalink|Nishide (Shingon Buddhism)|Q20042042|Nisshu Shonin}} was ordered to rebuild the shrine, and on December 13, 3rd year of {{jalink|Eiroku|Q1143341}} ({{jalink|1560|Q6613}}), the shrine was moved to the newly constructed shrine building.{{Cite web |title=National Diet Library Digital Collection |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/992141/1/18 |website=dl.ndl.go.jp |access-date=2024-05-28}}. From {{jalink|Sengoku period (Japan)|Q204023|Sengoku period}} to {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}}, it was revered by the {{jalink|Shimadzu clan|Q1061406}}, the local {{jalink|Daimyo|Q61982}}.In {{jalink|1871|Q7746|1871}}{{jalink|year|Q577}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}4), it was ranked as a Kokuhei Chusha shrine as ``Shikajima Shrine'' in {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}} by the Meiji government. In {{jalink|1874|Q7761}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}7), the {{jalink|Jingu|Q120680118}} was declared and {{jali nk|Modern shrine rank system|Q712534}}, it was ranked as {{jalink|Kanpei Chusha}} and was promoted to Kanpei Taisha in {{jalink|1895|Q7844}} (Meiji 28). After the war, it became {{jalink|Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shinja Honcho|Q908077}}. {{jalink|1935|Q18658}} (Showa 10) {{jalink|November 10|Q2988}}, {{jalink|Emperor Showa|Q34479}}, who is participating in the {{jalink|Special Army Exercise}}, visits the train. |publisher=Shinchosha |year=2016-09-30 |page=77 |isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}.{{jalink|2021|Q49628}} ({{jalink|Reiwa|Q62609017}}3) November 19th, National {{jalink|Cultural Council|Q1 1499811}} recommends that the main shrine, worship hall, imperial envoy hall, and main shrine of Sessha Shisho Shrine be designated as {{jalink|Important Cultural Properties|Q1188622}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kokuho-jubun.html |title=About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) |publisher=Kirishima City |date=2021-10-29 |accessdate=2022-02-11}}. The following year, it was announced in {{jalink|Official Gazette|Q11452096}} on February 9, 2022, and it was officially designated as an important cultural property.{{cite news|title=Kirishima Shrine officially designated as a national treasure. Kagoshima Shrine also designated as an important cultural property |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209055427/https://www3.nhk.or.jp/lnews/kagoshima/20220209/5050017814.html |publisher= {{jalink|Japan Broadcasting Corporation|Q212128}} (NHK NEWS WEB) |date=2022-02-09 |accessdate=2022-02-11}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|date=2022-02-09 |url=http://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kokuhoukettei.html |title=About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) |publisher=Kirishima City |accessdate=2022-02-11}}. === Enshrinement of Hachiman God === It is also said that in the {{jalink|Heian period|Q193292}}, when {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} solicited the Yawata Bekku shrines of the five places in Kyushu, the {{jalink|Hachiman deity|Q261637}} was enshrined in our company. Since then, it has also been called Sho Hachiman Shrine, Osumi Sho Hachiman Shrine, {{jalink|Kokufu Hachiman Shrine|Q11420856|Kokubu Hachiman Shrine}}. In the "{{jalink|Konjaku Monogatari Shu|Q1507085}}" compiled in the late Heian period, {{jalink|Hachiman God|Q261637}} is {{jalink|Osumi Province|Q981002} }, then moved to {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa}}, and finally left its mark at {{jalink|Iwashimizu Hachimangu|Q710098|Iwashimizu}}.{{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q 329792}}5 ({{jalink|544|Q31012}}), it is said that {{jalink|Hachimanjin|Q261637}} was worshiped at this former shrine. ``When Ohirume, the daughter of the great king of Shintan Province ({{jalink|China|Q29520}} as seen from {{jalink|India|Q668}}), was seven years old, the morning sun pierced her chest, she became pregnant and gave birth to a prince.The king's retainers became suspicious of this, put her on an empty ship, and took the place where the ship was as their territory. The ship eventually arrived at a rocky shore in Chinzei, Japan, and the prince was named Hachiman.It is said that this was during the reign of Emperor Keitai. Furthermore, in ``{{jalink|Shrine Enlightenment}}'' written by {{jalink|Shirai Soin}}, the character is listed as ``Chen the Great,'' and his daughter's name is said to be Hachiman.Kagoshima Shrine is also said to be the original headquarters of Hachiman Shrine, as indicated by the positive character of Osumi Sho Hachiman. Legend has it that there was once a dispute between Kokubun Hachiman and {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} over which one was the legitimate Hachiman, and {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} secretly sent 15 (all 14) messengers to burn down Kokubun Hachiman. At that time, the character ``Sho Hachiman'' appeared in the black smoke rising from the burning shrine, and the messengers, shocked and frightened by this, fled to the land of {{jalink|Mizobe Town|Q11564513|Mizobe}}, but as if they had been punished by God, they fell down one after another, reaching 13 people in number. Afterwards, the local people took pity on those who died in a foreign land, and built mounds at the places where each of them had fallen to comfort the spirits.Since there were 13 mounds, it is said that they named the place {{jalink|Jusanzukahara|Q11404752}}. This {{jalink|Jusanzukahara|Q11404752}} is located in the north of {{jalink|Kokubu Plain|Q11420534}} of {{jalink|Kagoshima Prefecture|Q15701}}, and in the northeast of it there is {{jalink|Kagoshima Airport|Q1156310}} and Jusanzukahara Historical Park based on this legend. There are several other legends about the messenger of {{jalink|Usa Shrine|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} that differ from the above. === Precincts === [[File:Sangoku meisho zue Kagoshima Shrine.jpg|Thumbnail|450x450 pixels|Kagoshima Shrine in the Edo period ("{{jalink|Sangoku Scenic View|Q11354726}}"). ]] * Otorii - Torii that straddles a public road * Dedicated wooden horse - A sacred horse (wooden horse) dedicated in 1945.According to the information board installed on site. . * Shinbasha * Chozuya* Main shrine, worship hall, imperial envoy hall - Important cultural properties. The shrine building, which was built in 1601, suffered severe damage from termites, so construction was started in 1755 with a donation from Shigetoshi Shimazu, and the construction was completed the following year under Shigego Shimazu{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shittebunkazai/bunka-hayato.html#5 |title=Kagoshima Shrine Main Hall and Worship Hall Imperial Mission Hall Sessha Shisho Shrine Main Hall |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kirishima City Hall Education Department Social Education Division Cultural Properties Group}}. The imperial envoy hall corresponds to the entrance to the main shrine building, and is lined up with the worship hall and main shrine on the north side. Each building has rich decorations, with a dragon carried in the hall of imperial envoys and a ceiling painting in the hall of worship.The main hall is extremely large, and the whole is decorated with carvings and murals by Tangen Kimura, a painter of the Satsuma domain.It is finished in rich colors and lacquer, and a dragon carving is wrapped around the pillar of the prayer hall.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.kagoshima.jp/ba08/documents/62592_20220210110955-1.pdf |title=Kagoshima Jingu Main Hall and Worship Hall, Imperial Envoy Hall, Sessha Shisho Shrine Main Hall |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture |format=PDF}}. Furthermore, this {{jalink|Dragon Pillar|Q60985310}} has four claws, making it unique compared to other shrines in southern Kyushu that have dragon pillars that have three claws.* Rebuilt stone lantern at the main shrine - Prefecturally designated tangible cultural property. A lantern donated to the main shrine (currently Kagoshima Jingu) in 1756. It is a stone lantern with two legs and is called a ``kotobashira lantern''. |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kirishima City Hall Education Department Social Education Division Cultural Properties Group}}. On the front side of the leg, there is an inscription about the construction of the shrine . * Kanda * Sacred Tree - {{jalink|Kenkyu|Q1193933|Kenkyu Year}} The tree is said to be about 800 years old. * Kameishi * Hayato History and Folklore Museum - There is a history exhibition room, a folklore exhibition room, and a Japanese-style room. Documents related to Kagoshima Jingu Shrine, archaeological materials such as earthenware and stone axes excavated in Hayato Town, and materials and folk tools related to local performing arts such as the bell-kake horse dance are displayed, and the Japanese-style room recreates the atmosphere of the Showa era.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/shisetsu/kyoiku/028.html |title=Hayato History and Folklore Museum |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kirishima City Hall}}. * Shrine office * Yoseikan === Setsusha === * Shisho Shrine - Important cultural property. Enshrined deities: {{jalink|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|Daisaku no Mikoto}}, {{jalink|Ishihime no Mikoto|Q11585498|Ishihime no Mikoto}}, Arata Rōme, Netori no Mikoto. Annual festival: November 15th. * Takeuchi Shrine - Enshrined deity: Takeuchi Sukune. * Hayabusa Shrine - Enshrined deity: Nihon Takemyo. * Sannosha - Three shrines are built in front of the torii gate at the entrance to the shrine grounds. * Mikado Shrine - Two shrines are built at the foot of the stone steps to the shrine grounds. * Amenosha - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Watatsumi|Q1474187|Toyotamahiko no Mikoto}}. Regular festival: October 11th. * Shokonsha * Inari Shrine * Yamakami Shrine * Otarachi Goddess Shrine * Takachiho Shrine Ruins/Ishitama Shrine - The former shrine of Kagoshima Jingu. This is where the main hall of Takachiho Palace was located. * Hoshoku Shrine === Gallery === File:Kagoshima-jingu, shaden.jpg|alt=|Shrine

{{small|Kagoshima Jingu Motomiya traditional site. }} File:Kagoshima-jingu, Kuwahatashi-yakata-ato.jpg|Shake Kuwahatashi House Ruins (among national historic sites) File:Kagoshima-jingu, Mirokuin-ato.jpg|Mirokuin ruins (among national historic sites) === Festival === [[File:Hatsu uma sai 02.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Hatsuuma sai (photographed in 2012)]] The annual festivals held at Kagoshima Shrine are as follows. . * Seven Kinds Festival (January 7th) * {{jalink|Hatsuuma Festival (Kagoshima Shrine)|Q11396442|Hatsuuma Festival}} (January 18th of the lunar calendar: In recent years, it has been a recent Sunday) * Fuji Festival (March 10th of the lunar calendar) * Rice planting festival (May 5th of the lunar calendar) * Annual festival (August 15th of the lunar calendar) * Tanabata Festival * Mihama Kudari Festival (3rd Sunday in October) === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Kagoshima Shrine 3 buildings (1 attached ridge tag) (buildings) - Construction began in 1755 with a donation from {{jalink|Shimadzu Shigetoshi|Q11476823}}. It was completed the following year during the reign of {{jalink|Shigego Shimazu|Q8013051}}. Designated on February 9, 2022 (Reiwa 4)Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 10, February 9, 2022. [https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shitebunkazai/bunka-hayato.html#5 Cultural property [Hayato]] (Kirishima City homepage, updated on February 8, 2022). ** Main shrine and worship hall ** Imperial Envoy Hall ** Sessha Shisho Shrine Main Hall * Dark blue armor with helmet and large sleeves (craft) *: Dedicated by Yukihisa Kabayama, chief retainer of the Shimazu clan. Designated on March 31, 1953 {{Nationally designated cultural property database|201|5547|Navy blue armor with helmet and large sleeves/>}}. * Various Idomaru helmets with large sleeves (crafts) *: Dedicated by Takahisa Shimazu in 1558. {{jalink|Kagoshima Prefectural Historical Materials Center Reimeikan}} Stored. Designated on March 31, 1953 {{Nationally Designated Cultural Properties Database|201|5548|Various Idomaru (helmet with large sleeves)}}. * Various Idomaru helmets with large sleeves (crafts)*: Dedicated by Takahisa Shimazu in 1558. Stored at Tokyo National Museum. Designated on March 31, 1953{{Nationally designated cultural property database|201|5549|Various Idomaru (helmet with large sleeves/)}}. * Sword Mumei (Den Norishige) (craft) *: Its whereabouts were unknown after it was requisitioned by the Occupation Forces after the war, but a sword with matching characteristics was found in Australia in 2022.{{cite news|title=Former National Treasure Sword Found in Australia? GHQ requisitioned after the war, whereabouts unknown |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220223195910/https://www3.nhk.or.jp/news/html/20220224/k10013498361000.html |publisher=Japan Broadcasting Corporation (NHK NEWS WEB) |date=2022-02-24 |accessdate=2022-03-03}}. Designated on April 8, 1918 (Taisho 7) {{Nationally Designated Cultural Properties Database|201|10468|Sword }}. * Sword, famous Sōshū Sumiakihiro Meitokusan (craft)*: Written in 1392. Dedicated by the 27th Shimazu Saioki. After the war, it was confiscated by the Occupation Forces and its whereabouts were unknown, but it was discovered at an auction and bought back by the shrine in 2003. Currently stored at Reimeikan, Kagoshima Prefectural Historical Materials Center. Designated on April 25, 1927. === National Historic Site === * Osumi Sho Hachiman Shrine Precincts and Shrine Remains - Designated on October 17, 2013 {{Nationally Designated Cultural Properties Database|401|00003825|Osumi Sho Hachiman Shrine Precincts and Shrine Remains}}. === Intangible folk cultural properties selected by the country{{jalink|Intangible folk cultural properties for which measures such as recording should be taken|Q11642584}} === * {{jalink|Hatsuuma Festival (Kagoshima Shrine)|Q11396442|Customs of horse dance in Satsuma}} - Selected on February 12, 2002 (Heisei 14){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/312/753 |title=Customs of horse dance in Satsuma / Intangible folk cultural properties for which measures such as recording should be taken |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Nationally designated cultural properties database / Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. === Cultural property designated by Kagoshima Prefecture === *Tangible cultural property ** Stone lantern (structure) in the main shrine reconstruction **: Designated on April 22, 2014 . ** Ceramics (crafts) owned by Kagoshima Jingu Shrine **: On March 25, 2008, it was designated as a Kirishima City-designated tangible cultural property (craft) as "Kagoshima Shrine Treasure Ceramics," and on April 23, 2010, it was designated as a Kagoshima Prefecture-designated tangible cultural property . ** Kagoshima Shrine Documents (Ancient Documents) **: Letter of appointment of Sho Hachiman Shrine priestess, letter of Seal of Sho Hachiman Shrine, letter of appointment of Seitoki Sakai for repair of the main shrine, letter of appointment of Tameharu Sakai of Hachiman Shrine repair office. Designated on March 16, 1987 [https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shittebunkazai/ichiran.html List of designated (registered) cultural assets] (Kirishima City homepage, updated on February 17, 2021). *Tangible folk cultural properties ** The god of rice fields in the shrine **: Designated on March 29, 1968 (Showa 43). === Kirishima City designated cultural property === *Tangible cultural property ** Hoshoku Shrine (building) at Tsuji-no-Kado - Originally Benzaiten-do Hall at Shirasagi Pond next to Miroku-in Temple. It was moved to its current location during the Meiji period during the Haibutsu-kishaku movement. Designated on July 6, 2005 . ** Kagoshima Jingu Four Heavenly Kings Stone Statues (Historical Materials) - Found at the Hayato History and Folklore Museum. Stored at Hayatozuka Historical Museum. Designated on June 7, 1994 . ** Jingu Old Seal (Historical Material) - Designated on July 3, 1995 . * Historic sites ** Miyasaka Shell Midden - A shell midden discovered on the back approach. Designated on December 8, 1999 . * Intangible folk cultural assets ** {{jalink|Hatsuuma Festival (Kagoshima Shrine)|Q11396442|Horse of the Eighteenth Day}} - Designated on March 31, 1987 (Showa 62) . Rice planting festival|Map = {{Location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kagoshima Shrine|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=12|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|frame-height=200|frame-latitude=31.751|frame-longitude=130.742}} }} [[File:Kagoshima-jingu, otorii.jpg|thumb|280px|right|{{center|Otorii}}]]'''Kagoshima Jingu'' (Kagoshima Jingu) is a shrine located in {{jalink|Kagoshima Prefecture|Q15701}}{{jalink|Kirishima City|Q858352}} Hayato Town. {{jalink|Shikinai Taisha|Q134917288}} ({{jalink|Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932|Kokuhei Taisha}}), {{jalink|Osumi Province|Q981002}}{{jalink|Ichinomiya|Q1656379}}. {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System#Government Shrine|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}, and currently it is {{jalink|Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shrine Head Office|Q908077}}. In the past, it was also called ``Osumi Sho Hachiman Shrine'' and ``Kokubu Hachiman Shrine.'' === Enshrined God === The current deities enshrined are as follows [http://kagoshima-jingu.jp/yuisyo.php About the history] (official website). . ; Main enshrined deity :* '''{{jalink|hoori|Q1051960|Amatsu Hidakahikohohodemi-no-mikoto}}''' :* '''{{jalink|Toyota Mahime|Q2329261|Toyota Hime no Mikoto}}''' (Toyota Hime no Mikoto) - Empress of Amatsu Hidakahiko Hidemi no Mikoto. ; Aidenjin :* {{jalink|Emperor Chuai|Q179971|Obichuhiko no Mikoto}} (Mikoto Nakatarashihiko, the 14th Emperor Chuai) :* {{jalink|Empress Jingu|Q232803|Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto}} (Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto, Empress Jingu) - Empress of Emperor Chuai. :* {{jalink|Emperor Ojin|Q317997|Shinada Wakeson}} (Mikoto Homuda, 15th Emperor Ojin, Hachiman Okami) :* {{jalink|Nakahime no Mikoto|Q11378496|Nakahime no Mikoto}} (Nakatsuhime no Mikoto, Nakahime no Mikoto) - Empress of Emperor Ojin. : The four pillars of Aidenjin are based on the relationship that {{jalink|Hachimanjin|Q261637}} is enshrined together. === History === According to the shrine's legend, it was founded in the distant {{jalink|the age of the gods|Q3577055}}, or ``during the reign of {{jalink|Emperor Jinmu|Q200188}}, it was built as a shrine at Takachiho-gu, which was the palace of {{jalink|Hoori|Q1051960|Amatsu Hidakahiko Hohoidemiko}}.'' It was moved to its current location in the first year of {{jalink|Wado|Q1373026}} ({{jalink|708|Q23511}}), and currently {{jalink|Setsusha|Q135009904}}'''Ishitai Shrine'' (Ishitai Shrine) is located on the former site. At a point 13km northwest of our company, there is {{jalink|Takayasanjo Mausoleum|Q11669273}}, which is said to be the {{jalink|Emperor's Mausoleum|Q17218816|Autumn}} of {{jalink|Hoori|Q1051960|Hoho Demikoto}}.The first appearance in reliable historical materials is in "{{jalink|Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932}}," which was compiled during the reign of Emperor Daigo|Q329753} as follows: Kagoshima Shrine" and is listed as a major shrine, and the so-called In {jalink|Southern Kyushu|Q8017707}}, it is the only {{jalink|Shikinai Taisha|Q134917288}} ({{jalink|Engishiki Jinmyocho|Q11064932|Kokuhei Taisha}}). Due to its high status, the Shinto priesthood produced influential {{jalink|national people|Q859955}} such as the {{jalink|Kuwahata clan}} and the {{jalink|Taxosho clan}}. In the {{jalink|Kenkyu|Q1193933|Kenkyu era}} (1190 - 1199), there was a company territory of over 2,500 {{jalink|town (unit)|Q1185752|machibu}}, and until the end of the Edo period, it had 1,000 {{jalink|stone height|Q909302|stone}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/tanbou/28/ |title=Kagoshima Shrine |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefectural Shrine Agency}}.{{jalink|Oei|Q1193564}} 7 ({{jalink|1527|Q6412}}) Because it was destroyed by military fire, {{jalink|astronomical (era name)|Q1192853|Tenbun}} In the 20th year ({{jalink|1551|Q6560}}), {{jalink|Emperor Konara|Q349467}} obtained {{jalink|reji|Q11607250}}, and {{jalink|Takahisa Shimazu|Q2367308}} became {{jalink|Nishide (Shingon Buddhism)|Q20042042|Nisshu Shonin}} was ordered to rebuild the shrine, and on December 13, 3rd year of {{jalink|Eiroku|Q1143341}} ({{jalink|1560|Q6613}}), the shrine was moved to the newly constructed shrine building.{{Cite web |title=National Diet Library Digital Collection |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/992141/1/18 |website=dl.ndl.go.jp |access-date=2024-05-28}}. From {{jalink|Sengoku period (Japan)|Q204023|Sengoku period}} to {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}}, it was revered by the {{jalink|Shimadzu clan|Q1061406}}, the local {{jalink|Daimyo|Q61982}}.In {{jalink|1871|Q7746|1871}}{{jalink|year|Q577}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}4), it was ranked as a Kokuhei Chusha shrine as ``Shikajima Shrine'' in {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}} by the Meiji government. In {{jalink|1874|Q7761}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}7), the {{jalink|Jingu|Q120680118}} was declared and {{jali nk|Modern shrine rank system|Q712534}}, it was ranked as {{jalink|Kanpei Chusha}} and was promoted to Kanpei Taisha in {{jalink|1895|Q7844}} (Meiji 28). After the war, it became {{jalink|Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shinja Honcho|Q908077}}. {{jalink|1935|Q18658}} (Showa 10) {{jalink|November 10|Q2988}}, {{jalink|Emperor Showa|Q34479}}, who is participating in the {{jalink|Special Army Exercise}}, visits the train. |publisher=Shinchosha |year=2016-09-30 |page=77 |isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}.{{jalink|2021|Q49628}} ({{jalink|Reiwa|Q62609017}}3) November 19th, National {{jalink|Cultural Council|Q1 1499811}} recommends that the main shrine, worship hall, imperial envoy hall, and main shrine of Sessha Shisho Shrine be designated as {{jalink|Important Cultural Properties|Q1188622}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kokuho-jubun.html |title=About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) |publisher=Kirishima City |date=2021-10-29 |accessdate=2022-02-11}}. The following year, it was announced in {{jalink|Official Gazette|Q11452096}} on February 9, 2022, and it was officially designated as an important cultural property.{{cite news|title=Kirishima Shrine officially designated as a national treasure. Kagoshima Shrine also designated as an important cultural property |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209055427/https://www3.nhk.or.jp/lnews/kagoshima/20220209/5050017814.html |publisher= {{jalink|Japan Broadcasting Corporation|Q212128}} (NHK NEWS WEB) |date=2022-02-09 |accessdate=2022-02-11}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|date=2022-02-09 |url=http://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kokuhoukettei.html |title=About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings) |publisher=Kirishima City |accessdate=2022-02-11}}. === Enshrinement of Hachiman God === It is also said that in the {{jalink|Heian period|Q193292}}, when {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} solicited the Yawata Bekku shrines of the five places in Kyushu, the {{jalink|Hachiman deity|Q261637}} was enshrined in our company. Since then, it has also been called Sho Hachiman Shrine, Osumi Sho Hachiman Shrine, {{jalink|Kokufu Hachiman Shrine|Q11420856|Kokubu Hachiman Shrine}}. In the "{{jalink|Konjaku Monogatari Shu|Q1507085}}" compiled in the late Heian period, {{jalink|Hachiman God|Q261637}} is {{jalink|Osumi Province|Q981002} }, then moved to {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa}}, and finally left its mark at {{jalink|Iwashimizu Hachimangu|Q710098|Iwashimizu}}.{{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q 329792}}5 ({{jalink|544|Q31012}}), it is said that {{jalink|Hachimanjin|Q261637}} was worshiped at this former shrine. ``When Ohirume, the daughter of the great king of Shintan Province ({{jalink|China|Q29520}} as seen from {{jalink|India|Q668}}), was seven years old, the morning sun pierced her chest, she became pregnant and gave birth to a prince.The king's retainers became suspicious of this, put her on an empty ship, and took the place where the ship was as their territory. The ship eventually arrived at a rocky shore in Chinzei, Japan, and the prince was named Hachiman.It is said that this was during the reign of Emperor Keitai. Furthermore, in ``{{jalink|Shrine Enlightenment}}'' written by {{jalink|Shirai Soin}}, the character is listed as ``Chen the Great,'' and his daughter's name is said to be Hachiman.Kagoshima Shrine is also said to be the original headquarters of Hachiman Shrine, as indicated by the positive character of Osumi Sho Hachiman. Legend has it that there was once a dispute between Kokubun Hachiman and {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} over which one was the legitimate Hachiman, and {{jalink|Usa Jingu|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} secretly sent 15 (all 14) messengers to burn down Kokubun Hachiman. At that time, the character ``Sho Hachiman'' appeared in the black smoke rising from the burning shrine, and the messengers, shocked and frightened by this, fled to the land of {{jalink|Mizobe Town|Q11564513|Mizobe}}, but as if they had been punished by God, they fell down one after another, reaching 13 people in number. Afterwards, the local people took pity on those who died in a foreign land, and built mounds at the places where each of them had fallen to comfort the spirits.Since there were 13 mounds, it is said that they named the place {{jalink|Jusanzukahara|Q11404752}}. This {{jalink|Jusanzukahara|Q11404752}} is located in the north of {{jalink|Kokubu Plain|Q11420534}} of {{jalink|Kagoshima Prefecture|Q15701}}, and in the northeast of it there is {{jalink|Kagoshima Airport|Q1156310}} and Jusanzukahara Historical Park based on this legend. There are several other legends about the messenger of {{jalink|Usa Shrine|Q715632|Usa Hachiman}} that differ from the above. === Precincts === [[File:Sangoku meisho zue Kagoshima Shrine.jpg|Thumbnail|450x450 pixels|Kagoshima Shrine in the Edo period ("{{jalink|Sangoku Scenic View|Q11354726}}"). ]] * Otorii - Torii that straddles a public road * Dedicated wooden horse - A sacred horse (wooden horse) dedicated in 1945.According to the information board installed on site. . * Shinbasha * Chozuya* Main shrine, worship hall, imperial envoy hall - Important cultural properties. The shrine building, which was built in 1601, suffered severe damage from termites, so construction was started in 1755 with a donation from Shigetoshi Shimazu, and the construction was completed the following year under Shigego Shimazu{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shittebunkazai/bunka-hayato.html#5 |title=Kagoshima Shrine Main Hall and Worship Hall Imperial Mission Hall Sessha Shisho Shrine Main Hall |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kirishima City Hall Education Department Social Education Division Cultural Properties Group}}. The imperial envoy hall corresponds to the entrance to the main shrine building, and is lined up with the worship hall and main shrine on the north side. Each building has rich decorations, with a dragon carried in the hall of imperial envoys and a ceiling painting in the hall of worship.The main hall is extremely large, and the whole is decorated with carvings and murals by Tangen Kimura, a painter of the Satsuma domain.It is finished in rich colors and lacquer, and a dragon carving is wrapped around the pillar of the prayer hall.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.kagoshima.jp/ba08/documents/62592_20220210110955-1.pdf |title=Kagoshima Jingu Main Hall and Worship Hall, Imperial Envoy Hall, Sessha Shisho Shrine Main Hall |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture |format=PDF}}. Furthermore, this {{jalink|Dragon Pillar|Q60985310}} has four claws, making it unique compared to other shrines in southern Kyushu that have dragon pillars that have three claws.* Rebuilt stone lantern at the main shrine - Prefecturally designated tangible cultural property. A lantern donated to the main shrine (currently Kagoshima Jingu) in 1756. It is a stone lantern with two legs and is called a ``kotobashira lantern''. |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kirishima City Hall Education Department Social Education Division Cultural Properties Group}}. On the front side of the leg, there is an inscription about the construction of the shrine . * Kanda * Sacred Tree - {{jalink|Kenkyu|Q1193933|Kenkyu Year}} The tree is said to be about 800 years old. * Kameishi * Hayato History and Folklore Museum - There is a history exhibition room, a folklore exhibition room, and a Japanese-style room. Documents related to Kagoshima Jingu Shrine, archaeological materials such as earthenware and stone axes excavated in Hayato Town, and materials and folk tools related to local performing arts such as the bell-kake horse dance are displayed, and the Japanese-style room recreates the atmosphere of the Showa era.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/shisetsu/kyoiku/028.html |title=Hayato History and Folklore Museum |access-date=2022-07-12 |publisher=Kirishima City Hall}}. * Shrine office * Yoseikan === Setsusha === * Shisho Shrine - Important cultural property. Enshrined deities: {{jalink|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|Daisaku no Mikoto}}, {{jalink|Ishihime no Mikoto|Q11585498|Ishihime no Mikoto}}, Arata Rōme, Netori no Mikoto. Annual festival: November 15th. * Takeuchi Shrine - Enshrined deity: Takeuchi Sukune. * Hayabusa Shrine - Enshrined deity: Nihon Takemyo. * Sannosha - Three shrines are built in front of the torii gate at the entrance to the shrine grounds. * Mikado Shrine - Two shrines are built at the foot of the stone steps to the shrine grounds. * Amenosha - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Watatsumi|Q1474187|Toyotamahiko no Mikoto}}. Regular festival: October 11th. * Shokonsha * Inari Shrine * Yamakami Shrine * Otarachi Goddess Shrine * Takachiho Shrine Ruins/Ishitama Shrine - The former shrine of Kagoshima Jingu. This is where the main hall of Takachiho Palace was located. * Hoshoku Shrine === Gallery === File:Kagoshima-jingu, shaden.jpg|alt=|Shrine
